A duration budget a computation or handover must meet (the series symbol); qualifiers name the instance, as in \(\FallbackDeadline\), the latest permissible wait before the fallback must begin. A deadline stated as a clock instant is lowercase, \(\DeadlineInstant\) or \(\Glyph{t_{\text{deadline,stop}}}\).


\(\HandoverTimeout\)
Handover Timeout
\(\text{s}\)
Timer an arbiter sets for an unacknowledged handover, \(\HandoverTimeout = \max(0, \min(\HandoverTimeoutCeiling, \FallbackDeadline))\), where \(\HandoverTimeoutCeiling\) is the protocol ceiling.


\(\CommitmentInstant\)
Commitment Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant after which a receding-horizon plan’s prefix is committed and can no longer be replaced by a new proposal.


\(\HazardOnset\)
Hazard Onset
\(\text{s}\)
Instant at which a hazard first becomes physically present, the reference from which detection and stopping intervals are measured.







A lease is authority that lapses unless it is renewed. The book uses six kinds:









Lease
Symbol
Distinction




Execution lease
remaining \(\RemainingExecutionLease\)
Any authority an admitted command source holds to keep driving the actuators without renewal; it begins at admission, and its expiry invokes the state-matched fallback.


Chunk lease
\(\ChunkLease\)
The execution lease of the autonomous chunk policy, renewed by each admitted chunk; it enters \(\PrebrakeDelay\).


Manual lease
\(\ManualLease\)
The execution lease of a human operator in manual mode, renewed by authenticated heartbeats; it replaces the chunk lease in \(\PrebrakeDelay\) while the operator drives.


Administrative lease
\(\IntentAdministrativeLease\)
The host-silence bound inside an intent lease: how long the application processor may hold a goal without renewing it.


Intent lease
expiry \(\IntentLeaseExpiry\)
The record that grants a grounded target and effort ceilings, never a path; it expires at the earliest of its evidence horizon, its administrative lease, and its stopping deadline.


Hardware lease
(mechanism)
The countdown timer on the safety microcontroller that enforces any of these expiries even when the process that issued the authority has hung.







In a serial model without overlap, one evaluation of a learned proposer on the robot’s onboard accelerator takes a time that splits into three terms: moving bytes through memory, executing operations, and a fixed overhead. The chunk-cadence and proposer-inference relationships below reuse these symbols, with a subscript naming the instance (\(\SustainedMemoryBandwidth\), \(\PrefillOperations\)):
\[\Time = \underbrace{\frac{\DataVolume}{\Bandwidth}}_{\text{Memory Time}} + \underbrace{\frac{\Operations}{\PeakRate \cdot \EfficiencyHw}}_{\text{Compute Time}} + \underbrace{\Latency}_{\text{Latency Overhead}}\]










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\Time\)
Execution Time
seconds
Total execution time of one evaluation; bare \(\Glyph{T}\) is always time.


\(\Bandwidth\)
Bandwidth
bytes/s
Sustained bytes per second across a named path; never bare \(\Glyph{B}\), which is batch size \(\BatchSize\).


\(\DataVolume\)
Data Volume
bytes
Bytes moved through memory in one evaluation; never bare \(\Glyph{D}\), which is dataset size.


\(\EfficiencyHw\)
Efficiency
—
Fraction of the peak rate an evaluation achieves, \(0 \le \EfficiencyHw \le 1\); never bare \(\Glyph{\eta}\), which is the learning rate.


\(\Latency\)
Latency
seconds
Fixed overhead per evaluation (kernel launch, transfer setup); the subscript keeps it distinct from the loss \(\LossFunction\).


\(\Operations\)
Operations
FLOPs
Floating-point operations one evaluation executes; a subscript names the phase (\(\PrefillOperations\)). Asymptotic cost is \(\mathcal{O}(\cdot)\).


\(\PeakRate\)
Peak Rate
FLOP/s
Peak arithmetic rate of the processor at the stated precision; never bare \(\Glyph{P}\), which is parameter count.







Large neural policies that stream their weights from memory may exceed a kilohertz control period. Action chunking predicts an action trajectory of horizon \(\ActionChunkHorizon\) at a lower cognitive frequency \(\Glyph{f_{\text{policy}}}\), while the chunk’s waypoints are consumed at \(\ActionExecutionRate\). In the serial model with one weight-streaming pass per chunk and no additional fixed overhead, memory streaming must fit inside the chunk execution window after reserving the compute term \(\Glyph{T_{\text{compute}}}\) of the single-device decomposition:
\[\ParameterStreamingTime = \frac{\WeightMemory}{\SustainedMemoryBandwidth} \le \frac{\ActionChunkHorizon}{\ActionExecutionRate} - \Glyph{T_{\text{compute}}}\]
A decoder that streams its nonresident weights once per emitted token spends, for \(\EmittedTokenCount\) emitted tokens, the inference time
\[\ProposerInferenceTime \approx \max\!\left(\frac{\PrefillOperations}{\EfficiencyHw\,\PeakRate},\ \frac{\WeightMemory}{\SustainedMemoryBandwidth}\right) + (\EmittedTokenCount - 1)\,\frac{\WeightMemory}{\SustainedMemoryBandwidth}\]
which caps the fresh-evaluation rate at \(\ProposerEvaluationRate \le \SustainedMemoryBandwidth/\WeightMemory\) when every evaluation streams the weights. The symbols are those of the single-device decomposition: \(\PrefillOperations\) counts the prefill’s operations, \(\PeakRate\) is the processor’s peak rate at the activation precision, \(\EfficiencyHw\) is the fraction of it the prefill achieves, and \(\ArithmeticIntensity\) is the arithmetic intensity that decides which term binds.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\ActionChunkHorizon\)
Horizon
Time steps
Number of contiguous future action steps generated in a single policy forward pass (\(\ActionChunkHorizon=16\) on the mobile manipulator; 16 to 64 steps in the literature).


\(\ActionDimension\)
Action Dimension
Integer
Number of components of one action \(\CognitivePolicyAction_{t}\); a chunk \(\Glyph{\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}}\) has \(\ActionChunkHorizon \times \ActionDimension\) entries.


\(\SustainedMemoryBandwidth\)
Sustained Memory Bandwidth
bytes/s
Achievable memory throughput of the SoC or accelerator memory subsystem (e.g., LPDDR5, HBM); the core’s \(\Bandwidth\) at the memory interface.


\(\ParameterStreamingTime\)
Parameter Streaming Time
\(\text{ms}\)
Time required to stream non-resident model weights into execution registers.


\(\ActionExecutionRate\)
Action Execution Rate
\(\text{Hz}\)
Temporal consumption rate of chunked waypoints along the planned trajectory (\(100\text{ Hz}\) to \(1\text{ kHz}\)).


\(\EmittedTokenCount\)
Emitted Token Count
tokens
Output tokens an autoregressive decoder emits per evaluation; the core’s sequence length \(\SequenceLength\) for the decoded part. Never \(\Glyph{D}\), which is dataset size.







For the stopping-based safety envelope, the machine must retain enough clearance to arrest its approach before crossing the protected boundary. The relationship below specializes the resident stop to one-dimensional motion starting and ending at zero acceleration, with symmetric jerk ramps and a constant-deceleration segment. The stopping distance combines travel during the pre-brake delay with braking travel; the delay-budget inequality adds the spatial margins:
\[\StoppingDistance(\SpeedAtDetection) = \SpeedAtDetection\,\PrebrakeDelay + \ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection), \qquad \ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection) = \frac{\SpeedAtDetection^2}{2\CredibleBrakingDeceleration} + \frac{\SpeedAtDetection\,\CredibleBrakingDeceleration}{2\JerkLimit} \quad (\SpeedAtDetection \ge \CredibleBrakingDeceleration^2/\JerkLimit)\]










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\StoppingDistance\)
Stopping Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Distance required to bring the plant to rest from speed \(\SpeedAtDetection\).


\(\StoppingDuration\)
Stopping Duration
\(\text{s}\)
Elapsed time from braking onset to standstill in the protective-separation calculation; distinct from controller sampling period.


\(\ClearDistance\)
Clear Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Clear distance from the machine to the boundary it must not cross; the subscript keeps it distinct from dataset size \(\Glyph{D}\).


\(\SpeedAtDetection\)
Speed at Detection
\(\text{m/s}\)
Speed of the machine at the moment the hazard is detected; in stopping, pre-brake, and impact algebra, the scalar travel or approach speed \(\SpeedAtDetection\).


\(\SpeedBound\)
Speed Bound
\(\text{m/s}\)
Largest speed the machine, a tracked object, or an approaching body is credited with in a budget; the bounding speed in \(\TelemetryFreshnessBound \le \PositionErrorCeiling/\SpeedBound\).


\(\CredibleBrakingDeceleration\)
Credible Deceleration
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Validated low tail of the deceleration the machine achieves under its stated conditions, not the datasheet peak.


\(\ProfileAccelerationBound\)
Profile Acceleration Bound
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Largest acceleration or deceleration a planned or interpolated profile may command; for the base’s resident stop it is set to \(\CredibleBrakingDeceleration\).


\(\NetBrakingDeceleration\)
Net Braking Deceleration
\(\text{m/s}^2, \text{rad/s}^2\)
Linear or angular deceleration left after a gravity or load bias torque \(\Glyph{\tau_{\text{bias}}}\) is subtracted from the actuator’s braking capacity, in the direction of travel.


\(\ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection)\)
Resident Stop Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Travel of the resident stop from speed \(\SpeedAtDetection\): \(\SpeedAtDetection^2/(2\CredibleBrakingDeceleration)\) for constant-deceleration braking; for the jerk-limited stop of equation 11.17, that term plus the jerk ramps’ \(\SpeedAtDetection\,\CredibleBrakingDeceleration/(2\JerkLimit)\) once \(\SpeedAtDetection \ge \CredibleBrakingDeceleration^2/\JerkLimit\).


\(\LocalizationBound\)
Localization Bound
\(\text{m}\)
Bound on localization and state-estimation error.


\(\ProtectiveClearanceMargin\)
Protective Clearance
\(\text{m}\)
Fixed, nonzero protective clearance between the machine envelope and the boundary.


\(\TrackingErrorBound\)
Tracking-Error Bound
\(\text{m}\)
Bound on the deviation between the commanded and the executed trajectory, stated by the enforcement record.


\(\HumanWalkingSpeedBound\)
Human Walking-Speed Bound
\(\text{m/s}\)
Walking-speed bound for a person approaching the machine, used in the form its safety standard states.


\(\JerkLimit\)
Jerk Limit
\(\text{m/s}^3\)
Maximum rate of change of deceleration; sets the jerk ramps of the resident stop in \(\ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection)\) (equation 11.17) and bounds the bumpless-transfer window \(\BlendingTransitionWindow\).







At crossover frequencies well below the sampling frequency, holding discrete control commands constant over sampling period \(\SamplingPeriod = 1/\SamplingRate\) contributes approximately half a sample period of delay. With fixed modeled enforcer and fieldbus delays, the relationship below estimates phase-margin erosion; its phase-lag term is in radians, so all phase margins must use the same angular unit before subtraction:
\[\ZohTransportDelay = \frac{\SamplingPeriod}{2}, \qquad \DelayPhaseLag = \CrossoverFrequency \left( \frac{\SamplingPeriod}{2} + \EnforcerComputeTime + \CommandTransportTime \right), \qquad \Glyph{\text{PM}_{\text{net}}} = \text{PM}_{\text{plant}} - \DelayPhaseLag > 0\]










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\ZohTransportDelay\)
ZOH Transport Delay
\(\text{s}\)
Equivalent continuous delay introduced by discrete Zero-Order Hold reconstruction (\(\SamplingPeriod / 2\)).


\(\SamplingPeriod, \SamplingRate\)
Sampling Period and Rate
\(\text{s}, \text{Hz}\)
Discrete controller execution period and frequency (\(\SamplingRate = 1/\SamplingPeriod\)).


\(\EnforcerComputeTime\)
Enforcer Compute Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time the enforcer takes to evaluate its constraints within one control period; with \(\CommandTransportTime\) it adds to the ZOH delay.


\(\PureTransportDelay\)
Pure Transport Delay
\(\text{s}\)
A fixed delay in a feedback or communication channel, contributing phase lag \(\AngularFrequency \PureTransportDelay\) at frequency \(\AngularFrequency\).


\(\CrossoverFrequency\)
Open-Loop Crossover Frequency
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Frequency at which open-loop gain \(\lvert \OpenLoopTransferFunction(\ImaginaryUnit\CrossoverFrequency) \rvert = 1\) (\(0\text{ dB}\)).


\(\DelayPhaseLag\)
Phase Lag Degradation
\(\text{rad}\) / \(\text{deg}\)
Phase erosion at crossover (\(\DelayPhaseLag \approx 28.65^\circ \cdot (\CrossoverFrequency / \SamplingRate)\) from the hold alone) depleting closed-loop stability margin.







Actuators are constrained by copper winding heating, DC bus rail droop, and magnetic saturation. Sustainable torque output is governed by the coupled electromechanical balance, written per joint with scalar torque:
\[\DcBusVoltage = \PhaseInductance \frac{d\TorqueProducingCurrent}{d\TimeInstant} + \ElectricalResistance(\WindingTemperature)\, \TorqueProducingCurrent + \MotorBackEmfConstant \RotorAngularSpeed, \qquad \StatorThermalCapacitance \frac{d\WindingTemperature}{d\TimeInstant} = \TorqueProducingCurrent^2 \ElectricalResistance(\WindingTemperature) - \frac{\WindingTemperature - \AmbientTemperature}{\ThermalResistance}, \qquad \CommandedJointTorque = \GearboxTransmissionEfficiency \GearReductionRatio \MotorTorqueConstant \TorqueProducingCurrent\]










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\MotorTorqueConstant, \MotorBackEmfConstant\)
Torque and Back-EMF Constants
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m/A}, \text{V}\cdot\text{s/rad}\)
Motor electromechanical coupling constants linking winding current to rotor shaft torque and rotor speed to back-EMF voltage (\(\MotorTorqueConstant \approx \MotorBackEmfConstant\) in SI units).


\(\TorqueProducingCurrent\)
Torque-Producing Current
\(\text{A}\)
Quadrature-axis current of a field-oriented drive, \(\MotorTorque = \MotorTorqueConstant \TorqueProducingCurrent\). Bare \(\Glyph{I}\) is never a current, because the series core reserves it for arithmetic intensity.


\(\MotorPhaseRmsCurrent\)
Motor Phase RMS Current
\(\text{A}\)
RMS phase current driving the stator windings of a brushless PM motor; an uppercase \(\Glyph{I}\) with a subscript names an RMS value or rating.


\(\InstantaneousPhaseCurrent\)
Instantaneous Phase Current
\(\text{A}\)
Signed instantaneous electrical phase current, positive from inverter node into winding; distinct from RMS phase current and torque-producing dq current.


\(\ContinuousCurrent, \PeakCurrent\)
Continuous / Peak Current
\(\text{A}\)
RMS current ratings bounded by winding insulation class and inverter MOSFET dissipation.


\(\PhaseInductance, \PhaseResistance\)
Phase Inductance and Resistance
\(\text{H}, \Glyph{\Omega}\)
Stator winding inductance and DC resistance; they set \(\ElectricalTimeConstant = \PhaseInductance/\PhaseResistance\).


\(\ElectricalResistance(\WindingTemperature)\)
Temperature-Dependent Resistance
\(\Glyph{\Omega}\)
Stator copper resistance at winding temperature \(\WindingTemperature\): \(\ElectricalResistance(\WindingTemperature) = \ReferenceWindingResistance [1 + \CopperTemperatureCoefficient(\WindingTemperature - \CopperReferenceTemperature)]\) with \(\CopperTemperatureCoefficient = 0.00393\text{ K}^{-1}\).


\(\ThermalResistance\)
Thermal Resistance
\(\text{K/W}\)
Lumped thermal resistance from stator windings to the ambient environment; path segments carry a second subscript (\(\JunctionAmbientThermalResistance\), \(\JunctionCaseThermalResistance\), \(\WindingCoreThermalResistance\), \(\CoreAmbientThermalResistance\)) and add in series.


\(\StatorThermalCapacitance\)
Stator Thermal Capacitance
\(\text{J/K}\)
Lumped heat capacity of the motor core, windings, and potting compound.


\(\ElectricalTimeConstant\)
Electrical Time Constant
\(\text{s}\)
Winding current rise time constant \(\ElectricalTimeConstant = \PhaseInductance/\PhaseResistance\); current reaches \(1 - e^{-1}\) of its target in \(\ElectricalTimeConstant\).


\(\ThermalTimeConstant\)
Thermal Time Constant
\(\text{s}\)
Actuator heating characteristic time constant (\(\ThermalTimeConstant = \ThermalResistance \StatorThermalCapacitance\), typically \(60\text{--}300\text{ s}\)); a single stage takes a second subscript (\(\CopperThermalTimeConstant\), \(\CaseThermalTimeConstant\)).


\(\WindingTemperature, \AmbientTemperature\)
Winding and Ambient Temperature
\(\text{K}\) or \(^\circ\text{C}\)
The thermal model’s state and boundary temperatures; the other temperatures follow the subscript rule of the disambiguation table (\(\JunctionTemperature\), \(\CaseTemperature\), \(\WindingTemperatureLimit\), \(\EquilibriumWindingTemperature\), \(\CopperReferenceTemperature\)).


\(\JouleanTemperatureRise\)
Joulean Temperature Rise
\(\text{K}\)
Thermal rise above ambient; \(\JouleanTemperatureRise = \WindingLossPower \ThermalResistance\) gives the steady-state rise for constant loss power in the lumped model. Transient rise follows the thermal balance; never a time interval.


\(\ActuatorDutyCycle\)
Actuator Duty Cycle
\([0, 1]\)
Ratio of active pulse duration to cycle period (\(\ActuatorOnTime / (\ActuatorOnTime + \ActuatorOffTime)\)) preventing thermal runaway.







Catastrophic failure rates in embodied systems cannot be certified through stochastic testing alone. For a defined hazard class \(\HazardClassIndex\), verified interception coverage and independently bounded residual faults constrain the system’s hazard rate. Under a constant-rate Poisson exposure model, zero-failure exposure follows the Rule of Three:
\[\SystemHazardRate \le \HazardousProposalRate (1 - \ShieldInterceptionCoverage) + \HardwareCommonCauseRate \le \TargetHazardRate, \qquad \FailureObservationInterval \ge \frac{-\ln \HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel}{\TargetHazardRate}\]
Here \(\FailureObservationInterval\) is the zero-incident operating exposure, in hours. For independent trials with a common success probability, per-trial campaigns use the same bound in probability form, \(\ZeroFailureTrialCount \ge \ln\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel/\ln \TargetTrialSuccessProbability \approx 3/(1 - \TargetTrialSuccessProbability)\).










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\SystemHazardRate\)
System Hazard Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Certified dangerous failure rate of the integrated cyber-physical machine for hazard class \(\HazardClassIndex\).


\(\HazardousProposalRate\)
Hazardous Proposal Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Arrival rate of unshielded hazardous action proposals the policy emits before the permission layer, measured against a counterfactual oracle.


\(\ShieldInterceptionCoverage\)
Shield Interception Coverage
Dimensionless
Verified conditional probability that the shield intercepts a hazardous proposal of class \(\HazardClassIndex\), evaluated over the states in which the policy errs.


\(\HardwareCommonCauseRate\)
Hardware and Common-Cause Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Independently bounded hardware-fault and common-cause hazard rate the shield cannot intercept; the floor \(\SystemHazardRate\) reaches when \(\ShieldInterceptionCoverage = 1\).


\(\TargetHazardRate\)
Target Hazard Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Tolerable dangerous failure rate assigned to the safety function by risk assessment, in the band its governing standard defines.


\(\DiagnosticCoverage\)
Diagnostic Coverage
Dimensionless
Rate-weighted fraction of hardware faults whose hazardous effect is mitigated, \(\UnmitigatedHardwareFaultRate = \RawHardwareFaultRate(1 - \DiagnosticCoverage)\); the hardware counterpart of \(\ShieldInterceptionCoverage\), which covers policy proposals.


\(\TrialFailureProbability, \TargetTrialSuccessProbability\)
Per-Trial Probabilities
Dimensionless
Per-trial failure probability, and the per-trial success probability a campaign must demonstrate; trial counts follow \(\ZeroFailureTrialCount \ge \ln\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel/\ln \TargetTrialSuccessProbability\).


\(\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel\)
Statistical Significance Level
Dimensionless
Type I error threshold (\(\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel = 1 - \text{CL}\), e.g., \(\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel=0.05\) for 95% confidence where \(-\ln(0.05) \approx 3.0\)).


\(\StatisticalFalseNegativeRate\)
Type II Error Allowance
Dimensionless
Probability of rejecting an acceptable candidate (\(1-\StatisticalFalseNegativeRate\) is the power); with \(\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel\) it sets the SPRT boundaries \(\SprtUpperBoundary\) and \(\SprtLowerBoundary\). Diffusion schedules use indexed \(\Glyph{\beta_s}\); a KL weight \(\Glyph{\beta}\) stays local to its objective.


\(\ZeroFailureTrialCount\)
Zero-Failure Trial Count
Trials
Required number of incident-free trials to substantiate \(\TargetTrialSuccessProbability\); for exposure measured in hours, the bound is on \(\FailureObservationInterval\) instead.


\(\SequentialLogLikelihoodRatio\)
Sequential Log-Likelihood Ratio
Dimensionless
After \(\ObservedTrialFailureCount\) failures in \(\SequentialTrialCount\) trials, \(\SequentialLogLikelihoodRatio = \ObservedTrialFailureCount\ln(\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_1/\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_0) + (\SequentialTrialCount-\ObservedTrialFailureCount)\ln\frac{1-\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_1}{1-\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_0}\) for per-trial failure probabilities \(\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_0\) (unacceptable) and \(\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability_1\) (acceptable); SPRT stops when it leaves \((\SprtLowerBoundary, \SprtUpperBoundary)\).


\(\SprtUpperBoundary, \SprtLowerBoundary\)
SPRT Boundaries
Dimensionless
Upper and lower stopping thresholds on \(\SequentialLogLikelihoodRatio\), \(\SprtUpperBoundary \approx \ln((1-\StatisticalFalseNegativeRate)/\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel)\) and \(\SprtLowerBoundary \approx \ln(\StatisticalFalseNegativeRate/(1-\HypothesisTestSignificanceLevel))\); never bare \(\Glyph{A}\) and \(\Glyph{B}\).


\(\AssuranceClaim\)
Assurance Claim
Proposition
Top-level safety claim of an assurance argument. Under an independent-premise probability model, its confidence \(\Pr(\AssuranceClaim)\) is the product of the premise confidences for a conjunctive argument, and one minus the product of the legs’ failure probabilities for a multi-legged one.







Untethered mobile manipulators and autonomous robots operate under strict battery energy reserves and peak thermal dissipation ceilings. Total mission energy (distinct from the ML workload’s \(\Glyph{E_{\text{total}}}\)) splits across mechanical actuation work, edge neural computation, and auxiliary sensor payloads. The compute energy expended by edge inference system-on-chip (SoC) devices decomposes into data movement and arithmetic operations according to the core energy corollary:
\[\MissionEnergy = \Glyph{E_{\text{act}}} + \Glyph{E_{\text{total}}} + \Glyph{E_{\text{aux}}}, \qquad \Glyph{E_{\text{total}}} \approx \DataVolume \times \Glyph{E_{\text{move}}} + \Operations \times \Glyph{E_{\text{compute}}}\]
For constant loss power in the single-node thermal model, resistive heating in stator windings \(\WindingLossPower \approx \sum \TorqueProducingCurrent^2 \ElectricalResistance(\WindingTemperature)\) sets the steady-state rise \(\JouleanTemperatureRise = \WindingLossPower \ThermalResistance\). Transient heating during shorter acceleration or contact bursts follows the coupled first-order thermal balance above.

title: Notation
text:
The symbols below describe the mechanical configuration, velocities, forces, and inertia of articulated and mobile mechanisms. Units for inertia and generalized loads specialize to revolute coordinates; mixed revolute–prismatic plants require entrywise units consistent with their generalized coordinates.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\PhysicalWorldState_{t} \in \WorldStateSpace\)
Physical World State
Mixed
Ground-truth continuous state of the machine, environment, and physical contacts at time \(\TimeInstant\), and the state of the decision process in the learning chapters; italic, because it mixes types.


\(\MechanicalPlantState\)
Mechanical Plant State
Mixed: \(\text{rad}\) or \(\text{m}\) for positions; \(\text{rad/s}\) or \(\text{m/s}\) for velocities
Generalized state vector \(\MechanicalPlantState = [\GeneralizedCoordinates^\top, \GeneralizedVelocities^\top]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{2\GeneralizedCoordinateCount}\) containing positions and velocities.


\(\GeneralizedCoordinates \in \mathbb{R}^\GeneralizedCoordinateCount\)
Generalized Coordinates
\(\text{rad}\) or \(\text{m}\)
Degrees of freedom describing mechanical articulation (joint angles and prismatic link extensions); entries \(\JointCoordinate_i\).


\(\GeneralizedVelocities \in \mathbb{R}^\GeneralizedCoordinateCount\)
Generalized Velocities
\(\text{rad/s}\) or \(\text{m/s}\)
First time derivative of generalized coordinates.


\(\GeneralizedAccelerations \in \mathbb{R}^\GeneralizedCoordinateCount\)
Generalized Accelerations
\(\text{rad/s}^2\) or \(\text{m/s}^2\)
Second time derivative of generalized coordinates.


\(\JointTorque \in \mathbb{R}^\GeneralizedCoordinateCount\)
Actuator Torque Vector
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\) or \(\text{N}\)
Generalized forces and torques delivered by actuators at mechanical joints; a subscript names a source, as in the contact torque \(\Glyph{\JointTorque_c}\).


\(\CommandedJointTorque\)
Commanded Joint Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Scalar torque commanded at one joint in single-joint derivations such as the kinetic barrier; bounds and disturbances keep a subscript (\(\JointTorqueLimit\), \(\Glyph{\tau_{\text{bias}}}\)).


\(\GeneralizedInertiaMatrix(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\)
Generalized Inertia Matrix
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)
Symmetric positive-definite mass/inertia matrix of the articulated multibody plant.


\(\CoriolisCentrifugalMatrix(\GeneralizedCoordinates, \GeneralizedVelocities)\)
Coriolis / Centrifugal Matrix
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{s/rad}\)
Matrix satisfying \(\Glyph{\dot{\mathbf{M}}} - 2\CoriolisCentrifugalMatrix\) skew-symmetry (passivity property).


\(\GravitationalTorqueVector(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\)
Gravitational Torque Vector
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Generalized gravitational load acting on links as a function of configuration; a single joint’s share is \(\Glyph{\tau_g}\).


\(\ManipulatorJacobian(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\)
Manipulator Jacobian
Mixed
Linear mapping \(\Glyph{\mathbf{v}_e} = \ManipulatorJacobian(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\GeneralizedVelocities\) from joint rates to operational task-space velocity.


\(\YoshikawaManipulability(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\)
Yoshikawa Manipulability
Depends on task coordinates and scaling
Singularity proximity metric \(\YoshikawaManipulability(\GeneralizedCoordinates) = \sqrt{\det(\ManipulatorJacobian\ManipulatorJacobian^\top)}\) vanishing at kinematic singular configurations.


\(\BackEmfVoltage\)
Back-EMF Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Opposing voltage \(\BackEmfVoltage = \MotorBackEmfConstant \RotorAngularSpeed\) developed across stator coils by rotor rotation.


\(\RotorInertia, \LoadInertia\)
Rotor and Load Inertia
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)
Moment of inertia of motor rotor shaft and coupled mechanical load.


\(\ReflectedRotorInertia\)
Reflected Rotor Inertia
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)
Effective inertia \(\ReflectedRotorInertia = \GearReductionRatio^2 \RotorInertia\) amplified quadratically by gearbox ratio.


\(\EffectiveJointInertia\)
Effective Joint Inertia
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)
Total inertia seen at one joint, link and payload plus \(\ReflectedRotorInertia\); the inertia in single-joint torque and acceleration budgets.


\(\GearReductionRatio\)
Gear Reduction Ratio
Dimensionless
Transmission reduction ratio (\(\GearReductionRatio = \RotorAngularSpeed/\JointAngularSpeed_j \gg 1\)) between motor rotor and joint output shaft; never bare \(\Glyph{N}\).


\(\InertiaMatchingRatio\)
Optimal Inertia-Matching Ratio
Dimensionless
Ratio \(\InertiaMatchingRatio = \sqrt{\LoadInertia / \RotorInertia}\) maximizing load angular acceleration under peak torque.


\(\GearboxTransmissionEfficiency\)
Transmission Efficiency
Dimensionless
Mechanical power transmission efficiency (\(0 < \GearboxTransmissionEfficiency \le 1\)); never bare \(\LearningRate\), which is the learning rate.


\(\PeakTorque, \HoldingTorque\)
Continuous / Peak / Holding Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Thermally continuous holding torque \(\HoldingTorque\) and transient peak acceleration torque.


\(\Mass\)
Mass
\(\text{kg}\)
Physical body or payload mass, lowercase italic; effective and reduced impact masses carry subscripts (\(\EffectiveImpactMass\), \(\ReducedImpactMass\)).


\(\Gravity\)
Gravitational Acceleration
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Scalar magnitude of gravitational acceleration; the vector \(\GravityVector\) and the configuration-dependent torque \(\GravitationalTorqueVector(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\) are bold.


\(\LinearMomentum\)
Linear Momentum
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}\)
Scalar momentum \(\Mass \BodySpeed\) of a moving body; distinct from the bold position \(\CartesianPosition\) and from a distribution \(\ProbabilityFunction(\cdot)\).


\(\WheelRadius\)
Wheel Radius
\(\text{m}\)
Rolling radius of a driven wheel, which converts wheel torque to floor force and speed to wheel rate (\(\Glyph{\omega} = \BodySpeed/\WheelRadius\)); the barrier relative degree \(\BarrierRelativeDegree\) appears only in barrier analysis.


\(\AngularSpeed\)
Angular Speed
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Magnitude of a rigid body’s angular velocity \(\AngularVelocity\); not the crossover frequency \(\Glyph{\omega_c}\).


\(\BaseForwardSpeed\)
Base Forward Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Forward linear speed of the mobile base along its heading, the speed input of the unicycle model; not the speed at the instant a hazard is detected.


\(\BaseHeadingRate\)
Base Heading Rate
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Rate of change of a mobile base’s heading angle, the turn input of the unicycle model.


\(\BaseLateralVelocity\)
Base Lateral Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Lateral velocity of a mobile base in the plane.


\(\BaseLongitudinalVelocity\)
Base Longitudinal Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Forward velocity of a mobile base in the plane.


\(\BodySpeed\)
Body Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Magnitude of the linear velocity of a moving body or machine; the scalar speed, with the vector velocity bold.


\(\CommandedJointTorqueSlew\)
Commanded Joint Torque Slew
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m/s}\)
Time derivative of the torque at a single joint; for constant effective inertia it equals \(\EffectiveJointInertia\) times the joint jerk.


\(\ContinuousTorque\)
Continuous Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Largest motor torque a winding can sustain indefinitely at its temperature limit under the stated cooling; set by heat rejection, and at the engineering ceiling it gives the installed rating.


\(\DirectAxisCurrent\)
Direct-Axis Current
\(\text{A}\)
Current of a field-oriented drive along the rotor field, which produces no torque and is normally regulated to zero; not the torque-producing quadrature current.


\(\ElectricalAngularSpeed\)
Electrical Angular Speed
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Rotor speed times the pole-pair count; the electrical frequency of the drive, not the mechanical shaft speed.


\(\ElectricalRotorAngle\)
Electrical Rotor Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Mechanical rotor angle times the pole-pair count, the angle a field-oriented drive uses to rotate between stator and rotor frames.


\(\EncoderAngle\)
Encoder Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Joint angle an encoder reports; a sample index appears as a subscript, as in \({\EncoderAngle}_{k}\).


\(\ForwardKinematicsMap\)
Forward Kinematics Map
Function
Map from joint positions to the positions of points on the robot’s links in the base frame.


\(\GeneralizedCoordinateCount\)
Generalized Coordinate Count
Dimensionless
Number of generalized coordinates of a mechanism, its degrees of freedom (the joints of a serial arm); the plant state has twice this many entries.


\(\HeadingAngle\)
Heading Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Heading of a planar mobile base in the unicycle model, the direction its forward speed points.


\(\ConveyorSpeed\)
Conveyor Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Speed of the belt that carries a workpiece past the pick station; not the bound on a takeaway conveyor, \(\ConveyorSpeedBound\).


\(\DrivenWheelLoadFraction\)
Driven-Wheel Load Fraction
Dimensionless
Fraction of a vehicle’s total weight carried by its driven wheels; it scales the traction ceiling on braking deceleration.


\(\JointCoordinate\)
Joint Coordinate
\(\text{rad}\) or \(\text{m}\)
One entry of the generalized coordinates \(\GeneralizedCoordinates\), a single joint’s angle or extension.


\(\JointPosition\)
Joint Position
\(\text{rad}\) or \(\text{m}\)
Position of a single joint along its axis, an angle for a revolute joint and a length for a prismatic one; its time derivatives are \(\JointVelocity\) and \(\JointAcceleration\).


\(\JointAngle\)
Joint Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Angle of one revolute joint, a scalar; the joint-space vector is \(\GeneralizedCoordinates\).


\(\JointVelocity\)
Joint Velocity
\(\text{rad/s}\) or \(\text{m/s}\)
Velocity of one joint, a scalar; the vector of all joints is \(\GeneralizedVelocities\).


\(\JointAngularSpeed\)
Joint Angular Speed
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Angular speed of a single arm joint; a subscript zero marks the initial value.


\(\JointAcceleration\)
Joint Acceleration
\(\text{rad/s}^2\) or \(\text{m/s}^2\)
Acceleration of one joint, a scalar; the vector of all joints is \(\GeneralizedAccelerations\).


\(\JointJerk\)
Joint Jerk
\(\text{rad/s}^3\)
Jerk of one joint’s trajectory, the third time derivative of its position; a scalar for one joint.


\(\JointCount\)
Joint Count
Dimensionless
Number of joints of a manipulator, the length of its joint-position vector; it shares its glyph with the zero-failure trial count of the validation chapters.


\(\JointIndex\)
Joint Index
Index
Position of one joint axis of a manipulator, from one to the number of joints.


\(\MotorTorque\)
Motor Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Torque a motor produces at its shaft before the transmission, the torque constant times the torque-producing current; the joint output is \(\JointOutputTorque\).


\(\JointOutputTorque\)
Joint Output Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Torque a joint delivers at the transmission output: the transmission efficiency \(\GearboxTransmissionEfficiency\) times the gear ratio \(\GearReductionRatio\) times the motor torque \(\MotorTorque\).


\(\JointFrictionTorque\)
Joint Friction Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Total friction torque of a joint, referred to its output link.


\(\JointTorqueLimit\)
Joint Torque Limit
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Largest torque the actuator of one joint can deliver, indexed by joint; it bounds \(\CommandedJointTorque\) at the same joint and is not the transient burst rating.


\(\JointTorqueUpperLimit\)
Joint Torque Upper Limit
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Per-joint upper bounds on the torque the actuators can deliver, as a vector; the vector counterpart of the scalar \(\JointTorqueLimit\).


\(\JointTorqueSlew\)
Joint Torque Slew
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m/s}\)
Time derivative of the joint torque vector; it couples to jerk through the derivative of the manipulator equation.


\(\JointVelocityLimit\)
Joint Velocity Limit
\(\text{rad/s}\) or \(\text{m/s}\)
Per-joint bounds on the magnitude of the generalized velocities; a planned trajectory and every admitted command must stay within them.


\(\JointTrackingError\)
Joint Tracking Error
\(\text{rad}\) or \(\text{m}\)
Vector of differences between the desired and the measured joint positions; not the state estimation error, which shares the glyph.


\(\LeverArmLength\)
Lever Arm Length
\(\text{m}\)
Distance from a rotating joint to the point it carries, which converts a joint rotation into tool travel; a scalar length.


\(\JacobianSingularNumber\)
Jacobian Singular Value
Mixed
Singular value of the manipulator Jacobian \(\ManipulatorJacobian\), the tool speed a unit joint rate produces along one singular direction; units follow the Jacobian rows.


\(\InverseKinematicsDamping\)
Inverse Kinematics Damping
Mixed
Damping length that damped-least-squares inverse kinematics adds to bound the joint step near a singularity; it enters squared, and along a singular direction the gain never exceeds one over twice its value. The ridge-regression analogue of weight decay.


\(\PermanentMagnetFluxLinkage\)
Permanent-Magnet Flux Linkage
\(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\)
Magnetic flux from the rotor magnets that links each stator winding; with the pole-pair count it sets the torque constant.


\(\PlantDynamicsFunction\)
Plant Dynamics Function
Function
Vector field of a plant’s equations of motion, giving the state rate from the state, the control input, and the plant parameters; not the unforced drift part of control-affine dynamics, which shares its glyph.


\(\PlantParameters\)
Plant Parameters
Record
Physical and hardware properties of the machine in one trial or rollout, such as tolerances, wear, payload mass, state of charge, and calibration; not the mass \(\Glyph{m}\) of a body.


\(\PlantStateRate\)
Plant State Rate
Dimensionless per unit time
Time derivative of the mechanical plant state; the decorated form of the plant state, and not the Cartesian velocity of the tool, which shares its glyph.


\(\PlantStateSpace\)
Plant State Space
Set
Set of all states the mechanical plant can occupy, positions together with velocities.


\(\RotorAngularSpeed\)
Rotor Angular Speed
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Angular speed of a motor rotor about its axis; it sets the back-EMF, and on a direct-drive hub motor it equals the wheel’s angular speed.


\(\RotorPolePairCount\)
Rotor Pole-Pair Count
Dimensionless
Number of magnetic pole pairs on a motor rotor; multiplying the mechanical rotor speed by it gives the electrical frequency of the drive.


\(\QuadratureAxisVoltage\)
Quadrature-Axis Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Voltage the inverter of a field-oriented drive applies along the quadrature axis, the axis that produces torque.


\(\TiltAngle\)
Tilt Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Angular deflection of a body from vertical; zero when the body is upright.


\(\TorqueRateLimit\)
Torque Rate Limit
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m/s}\)
Largest rate of change of joint output torque a drive accepts. Divided by the effective joint inertia it bounds joint jerk.


\(\TransmissionTorsionalStiffness\)
Transmission Torsional Stiffness
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m/rad}\)
Torsional stiffness of the transmission between rotor and output link, the compliance that couples motor to load.


\(\YawRate\)
Yaw Rate
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Angular velocity of a body about its vertical axis, one component of the body angular velocity \(\AngularVelocity\).

title: Notation
text:
Contact turns a free-moving body into a constrained one. The symbols here describe the forces a contact can transmit, the friction cone that bounds them, and the centroidal quantities that sum them over the whole robot.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\ActuationSelectionMatrix \in \mathbb{R}^{\GeneralizedCoordinateCount \times (\GeneralizedCoordinateCount+6)}\)
Actuation Selection Matrix
Matrix
Matrix \([\ZeroMatrix, \IdentityMatrix]\) projecting generalized forces onto actuated joints in floating-base systems.


\(\ContactPointForce_{k} \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Contact Force Vector
\(\text{N}\)
Physical contact force exerted by environment on contact patch \(\Glyph{k}\) (\(\ContactPointForce_{k} = [\TangentialContactShear^\top, \NormalContactForce]^\top\)); always indexed by the contact.


\(\FingerNormalForce\)
Finger normal force
N
Normal force one finger of a grasp presses against the object at its contact.


\(\FingerTangentialForce\)
Finger tangential force
N
Tangential friction force one finger of a grasp carries at its contact, bounded by the friction cone times \(\FingerNormalForce\).


\({\ContactPointJacobian}_k(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\)
Contact Point Jacobian
Mixed
Mapping joint velocities to contact patch Cartesian linear velocity: \(\Glyph{\dot{\mathbf{p}}}_k = {\ContactPointJacobian}_k(\GeneralizedCoordinates) \GeneralizedVelocities\).


\(\NormalContactForce\)
Normal Contact Force
\(\text{N}\)
Unilateral compressive force (\(\NormalContactForce = \ContactPointForce_{k}^\top \ContactNormal_k \ge 0\)) perpendicular to contact plane.


\(\TangentialContactShear\)
Tangential Contact Shear
\(\text{N}\)
Friction traction force tangential to contact plane (\(\TangentialContactShear = \ContactPointForce_{k} - \NormalContactForce \ContactNormal_k\)).


\(\CoulombFrictionCoefficient\)
Coulomb Friction Coefficient
Dimensionless
Static/kinetic coefficient bounding friction cone: \(\lVert \TangentialContactShear \rVert \le \CoulombFrictionCoefficient \NormalContactForce\).


\(\MassCenterPosition \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Center of Mass (CoM)
\(\text{m}\)
Spatial coordinates of the total articulated body mass centroid (\(\MassCenterPosition = \frac{1}{\Mass} \sum \Mass_i \CartesianPosition_i\)).


\(\CentroidalLinearMomentum\)
Centroidal Linear Momentum
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}\)
Total plant linear momentum (\(\CentroidalLinearMomentum = \Mass \Glyph{\dot{\mathbf{c}}}\)), governed by \(\CentroidalLinearMomentumDerivative = \sum \ContactPointForce_{k} + \Mass \GravityVector\), with gravitational acceleration \(\GravityVector\).


\(\CentroidalAngularMomentum\)
Centroidal Angular Momentum
\(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}\)
Angular momentum about CoM: \(\CentroidalAngularMomentumDerivative = \sum (\CartesianPosition_k - \MassCenterPosition) \times \ContactPointForce_{k} + \ContactPointTorque_k\).


\(\ZeroMomentPoint \in \mathbb{R}^2\)
Zero Moment Point (ZMP)
\(\text{m}\)
Ground-plane point where net horizontal tipping moment vanishes; must reside in \(\text{Conv}(\{\CartesianPosition_k\})\).


\(\RestitutionCoefficient \in [0, 1]\)
Coefficient of Restitution
Dimensionless
Kinematic velocity rebound ratio during non-smooth impact (\(\JointVelocity^+ = -\RestitutionCoefficient \JointVelocity^-\)).


\(\ContactStiffness, \HertzianContactStiffness\)
Contact Stiffness
\(\text{N/m}\)
Elastic stiffness of a structural contact, and of the human body region \(\Glyph{H}\) in an impact (with its effective mass \(\BodyRegionMass\)), in the form ISO/TS 15066 states.


\(\EffectiveImpactMass\)
Effective Impact Mass
\(\text{kg}\)
Apparent normal mass at a specified contact point and configuration. For a single frictionless normal impact, it is the reciprocal of the positive scalar Delassus coefficient formed from the contact normal Jacobian and generalized inertia matrix (Rigid Body Contact Mechanics).


\(\ReducedImpactMass\)
Reduced Impact Mass
\(\text{kg}\)
Two-body reduced mass of a collision, \(\ReducedImpactMass = (1/\EffectiveImpactMass + 1/\BodyRegionMass)^{-1}\), which sets the transferred energy.


\(\UnbrakedImpactForce\)
Unbraked Impact Force
\(\text{N}\)
Transient collision force peak (\(\UnbrakedImpactForce = \SpeedBound \sqrt{\HertzianContactStiffness \ReducedImpactMass}\)) governed by ISO/TS 15066.


\(\ArmStoppingDeceleration\)
Arm Stopping Deceleration
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Deceleration the arm must achieve after braking onset to stop within the latch force limit.


\(\BodyRegionMass\)
Body Region Mass
\(\text{kg}\)
Effective mass of a human body region, here the hand, in the ISO/TS 15066 body model.


\(\BrakeCommandForce\)
Brake Command Contact Force
\(\text{N}\)
Contact force against the latch at the instant the brake command issues, after the contact loop responds; distinct from a commanded traction force.


\(\BrakingOnsetContactForce\)
Braking Onset Contact Force
\(\text{N}\)
Contact force reached against the latch plate at physical braking onset.


\(\CentroidalAngularMomentumDerivative\)
Centroidal Angular Momentum Derivative
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Time derivative of the centroidal angular momentum, the net external moment about the center of mass: contact-force moments plus the contact torques.


\(\CentroidalLinearMomentumDerivative\)
Centroidal Linear Momentum Derivative
\(\text{N}\)
Time derivative of the centroidal linear momentum, the net external force on the robot: the sum of contact forces plus mass times gravity.


\(\ContactApproachSpeed\)
Contact Approach Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Speed at which the robot approaches and strikes a contact surface; contact force rises at stiffness times this speed.


\(\ContactDirectionVelocity\)
Contact Direction Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Velocity of the robot’s contact point along the contact direction.


\(\ContactForce\)
Contact Force
\(\text{N}\)
Force between the robot and the environment at a contact, along the contact direction; the per-point vector is \(\ContactPointForce_{k}\).


\(\ContactLoopResponseTime\)
Contact Loop Response Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time the contact-control loop takes to respond after its tripwire fires.


\(\ContactNormal\)
Contact Normal
Dimensionless
Unit vector normal to the contact plane at one contact, pointing into the robot; indexed by contact.


\(\ContactNormalPosition\)
Contact Normal Position
\(\text{m}\)
Position of a tool or link along the contact normal, whose change from first contact is the contact penetration in the spring contact model.


\(\ContactPointIndex\)
Contact Point Index
Index
Position of one contact point among the contacts of a grasp.


\(\ContactPointOffset\)
Contact Point Offset
\(\text{m}\)
Position of a grasp contact relative to the reference point of the grasped object, the moment arm of its force; indexed by contact.


\(\ContactPointPosition\)
Contact Point Position
\(\text{m}\)
Position of the robot’s contact point along the contact direction.


\(\ContactPointTorque\)
Contact Point Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Moment the environment exerts on the robot at one contact patch, the torque part of the contact wrench; indexed by contact. Not the joint torque vector \(\JointTorque\), which shares the glyph.


\(\ContactTripwireForce\)
Contact Tripwire Force
\(\text{N}\)
Contact force at which the permission path ends an attempt on the machine, set below the structural damage limit.


\(\ContactWrench\)
Contact Wrench
Varies
Force and moment the environment applies at a contact, stacked into one vector; force rows in newtons, moment rows in newton-meters. Privileged in simulation.


\(\ContactWrenchCeiling\)
Contact Wrench Ceiling
Varies
Largest contact force and torque an intent lease permits at the tool, stacked as a wrench; units mix newtons and newton-meters.


\(\DesiredContactPosition\)
Desired Contact Position
\(\text{m}\)
Setpoint position of the robot’s contact point along the contact direction.


\(\DesiredContactVelocity\)
Desired Contact Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Setpoint velocity of the robot’s contact point along the contact direction.


\(\EffectiveSeriesStiffness\)
Effective Series Stiffness
\(\text{N/m}\)
Stiffness of a contact whose two sides deflect in series, the reciprocal of the sum of their compliances; the softer side dominates.


\(\ExternalWrench\)
External Wrench
Mixed
Force and moment the environment applies at the end effector, in newtons for the force and newton-meters for the moments; it maps into joint torques through the transposed manipulator Jacobian.


\(\ExternalContactTorque\)
External Contact Torque Vector
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Joint torques produced by external contact forces acting on the manipulator.


\(\ExternalJointTorque\)
External Joint Torque
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)
Torque the environment applies at one joint’s output; the scalar counterpart of the external contact torque vector \(\ExternalContactTorque\).


\(\FrictionCoefficientFloor\)
Friction Coefficient Floor
Dimensionless
Lowest friction coefficient a braking or contact premise assumes the surface provides; an unobserved oil spill can invalidate it.


\(\GraspForceCeiling\)
Grasp Force Ceiling
\(\text{N}\)
Largest grasp contact force the object tolerates without crushing or deforming.


\(\GraspForceFloor\)
Grasp Force Floor
\(\text{N}\)
Smallest grasp contact force that holds the object against slip; the grasp must stay between this floor and \(\GraspForceCeiling\).


\(\GraspMap\)
Grasp Map
Matrix
Linear map from contact forces to the wrench they exert on the grasped object; indexed by contact when one contact is meant; not the Kalman gain.


\(\GravityCenterHeight\)
Center-of-Gravity Height
\(\text{m}\)
Height of a vehicle’s center of gravity above the floor; it sets the tip-over ceiling on deceleration.


\(\GravityVector\)
Gravity Vector
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Gravitational acceleration as a vector pointing down with the magnitude of surface gravity; the scalar is the gravitational acceleration, and it is not the vector of gravitational joint torques.


\(\ImpedanceControlledPosition\)
Impedance-Controlled Position
\(\text{m}\)
Measured position of the point an impedance controller regulates; its deviation from \(\ImpedanceEquilibriumPosition\), times the stiffness, is the spring term.


\(\ImpedanceControlledVelocity\)
Impedance-Controlled Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Measured velocity of the regulated point, the time derivative of \(\ImpedanceControlledPosition\).


\(\ImpedanceEquilibriumPosition\)
Impedance Equilibrium Position
\(\text{m}\)
Virtual rest point of the emulated spring that an impedance controller pulls the controlled point toward.


\(\ImpedanceEquilibriumVelocity\)
Impedance Equilibrium Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Velocity of the virtual equilibrium; its difference from \(\ImpedanceControlledVelocity\), times the damping, is the damper term.


\(\KineticEnergy\)
Kinetic Energy
\(\text{J}\)
Energy a moving body carries, one half its mass times its speed squared (plus rotational terms where stated); not the standard’s limit on energy transferred to a person.


\(\MassCenterHeight\)
Center-of-Mass Height
\(\text{m}\)
Height of a body’s center of mass above its support or contact point; it sets the natural frequency of the linear inverted pendulum, \(\sqrt{\Gravity/\MassCenterHeight}\), and is not a camera-frame coordinate.


\(\PenetrationDepth\)
Penetration Depth
\(\text{m}\)
Depth by which one body penetrates or compresses another at a contact, measured along the contact normal; penalty and compliant contact models compute normal force from it. Shares its glyph with the Huber threshold of the training chapters.


\(\PenetrationRate\)
Penetration Rate
\(\text{m/s}\)
Time rate of change of the penetration depth \(\PenetrationDepth\) at a contact; zero at the instant of maximum compression.


\(\LatchApproachSpeed\)
Latch Approach Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Speed at which the arm presses into the cage-door latch plate; the enforcement and release chapters use the same latch scenario.


\(\LatchForceLimit\)
Latch Force Limit
\(\text{N}\)
Structural force limit of the door latch the arm pushes against.


\(\LatchPlateStiffness\)
Latch Plate Stiffness
\(\text{N/m}\)
Spring stiffness of the cage-door latch plate the arm compresses.


\(\LeadingSupportDistance\)
Leading Support Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Horizontal distance from a vehicle’s center of gravity forward to its leading ground support; it shrinks when an arm extends forward.


\(\IntrusionDistance\)
Intrusion Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a body part can intrude past the sensing field before detection; a term of the ISO/TS 15066 protective separation distance.


\(\PersonApproachTravel\)
Person Approach Travel
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a person travels toward the robot during the robot’s reaction and stopping time; a term of the ISO/TS 15066 protective separation distance.


\(\PersonPositionUncertainty\)
Person Position Uncertainty
\(\text{m}\)
Position uncertainty of the person from the sensing system; a term of the ISO/TS 15066 protective separation distance.


\(\KnownComponentStopDistance\)
Known-Component Stop Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Stopping travel that the known components of the stopping budget add up to at a given speed on a dry floor: delay travel, braking, jerk ramps, and fixed overheads; the clear distance minus it is the spare the stopping claim holds in reserve.


\(\PreImpactNormalVelocity\)
Pre-Impact Normal Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Normal contact velocity just before an impact, negative while the bodies approach; the restitution law links it to the post-impact velocity.


\(\PostImpactNormalVelocity\)
Post-Impact Normal Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Normal contact velocity just after an impact, equal to minus the restitution coefficient times the pre-impact normal velocity.


\(\RobotStructuralStiffness\)
Robot Structural Stiffness
\(\text{N/m}\)
Stiffness of the manipulator side of a contact, its pads, linkages, and joint elasticity acting as one series spring; it combines in series with the stiffness of the struck body.


\(\SlipAccelerationBound\)
Slip Acceleration Bound
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Bound on the residual acceleration of a tracked object slipping relative to its carrier; it widens the evidence horizon of a target estimate.

title: Notation
text:
Every measurement a robot uses arrives in some frame, and every command leaves in another. These symbols name the frames, the rigid transforms between them, and the camera models that project the world onto a sensor.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\SpecialEuclideanGroup\)
Special Euclidean Group
Lie Group
Group of 3D rigid-body spatial transformations (translations and rotations: \(\mathbb{R}^3 \rtimes \SpecialOrthogonalGroup\)).


\(\SpecialOrthogonalGroup\)
Special Orthogonal Group
Lie Group
Group of \(3 \times 3\) proper orthogonal rotation matrices (\(\DirectionalCosineMatrix^\top \DirectionalCosineMatrix = \IdentityMatrix, \det(\DirectionalCosineMatrix) = +1\)).


\(\WorldReferenceFrame, \BodyReferenceFrame, \Glyph{\mathcal{F}_E}\)
Coordinate Reference Frames
Reference
Fixed World frame (\(\WorldReferenceFrame\)), mobile robot Base/body frame (\(\BodyReferenceFrame\)), and End-effector frame (\(\Glyph{\mathcal{F}_E}\)).


\(\CartesianPosition \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Cartesian 3D Position
\(\text{m}\)
Position vector \([\Glyph{x}, \Glyph{y}, \Glyph{z}]^\top\) expressing point coordinates in a stated frame.


\(\RigidTransformTranslation \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Rigid-Transform Translation
\(\text{m}\)
Translation part of a rigid transform between two frames (the offset of one frame’s origin in the other).


\(\DirectionalCosineMatrix \in \SpecialOrthogonalGroup\)
Directional Cosine Matrix
Matrix
\(3 \times 3\) orthonormal matrix parameterizing spatial attitude and orientation.


\(\UnitQuaternion \in \Glyph{\mathbb{H}}\)
Unit Quaternion
Dimensionless
Hypercomplex orientation vector \([\Glyph{w}, \Glyph{x}, \Glyph{y}, \Glyph{z}]^\top\) satisfying \(\lVert \UnitQuaternion \rVert = 1\).


\(\Pose \in \SpecialEuclideanGroup\)
Pose
Matrix
Rigid-body pose of a named frame, such as a grasp, the tool center point, or a target (\(\Glyph{\Pose_{\text{grasp}}}\), \(\Glyph{\Pose_{\text{TCP}}}\)); the transform between two frames is \(\HomogeneousTransform\) below.


\(\HomogeneousTransform \in \SpecialEuclideanGroup\)
Homogeneous Transform
Matrix
\(4 \times 4\) matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} \TransformRotationBlock & \TransformTranslationBlock \\ \ZeroVector^\top & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) mapping coordinates from frame \(\Glyph{B}\) into frame \(\Glyph{A}\).


\(\AngularVelocity, \AngularAcceleration \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Angular Velocity & Acceleration
\(\text{rad/s}, \text{rad/s}^2\)
Spatial angular velocity and angular acceleration vectors of a rigid body.


\(\SensorLeverArm \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
Sensor Lever-Arm Vector
\(\text{m}\)
Displacement vector from body rotation origin \(\Glyph{O}\) to displaced sensor location \(\Glyph{P}\); its length, or a link’s lever arm, is the scalar \(\LeverArmLength\).


\(\FundamentalMatrix, \EssentialMatrix\)
Fundamental and Essential Matrices
Matrix
Two-view epipolar constraint \(\HomogeneousPixelCoordinates_2^\top \FundamentalMatrix\HomogeneousPixelCoordinates_1 = 0\) with \(\EssentialMatrix = [\RigidTransformTranslation]_\times \DirectionalCosineMatrix\); the subscript keeps it distinct from the transition matrix \(\StateTransitionMatrix\).


\(\CameraIntrinsicCalibrationMatrix \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}\)
Pinhole Camera Intrinsics
Pixels
Calibration matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} \HorizontalFocalLength & 0 & \PrincipalPointColumn \\ 0 & \VerticalFocalLength & \PrincipalPointRow \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) parameterizing focal lengths and principal center.


\(\CameraIntrinsicInverseTranspose\)
Inverse-transpose intrinsic matrix
Matrix
Transpose of the inverse of the camera intrinsic matrix \(\CameraIntrinsicCalibrationMatrix\), which carries an essential matrix into the pixel-coordinate fundamental matrix.


\(\CameraFramePoint = [\CameraFrameHorizontalCoordinate, \CameraFrameVerticalCoordinate, \CameraFrameDepth]^\top\)
Camera-Frame 3D Coordinate
\(\text{m}\)
Metric coordinates of a spatial point in the optical camera frame (\(\CameraFrameDepth\) is optical depth).


\([\PixelColumnCoordinate, \PixelRowCoordinate]^\top\), \(\HomogeneousPixelCoordinates\)
Image Plane Pixel Coordinates
Pixels
Discrete sensor pixel coordinates (\(\PixelColumnCoordinate \sim \HorizontalFocalLength \frac{\CameraFrameHorizontalCoordinate}{\CameraFrameDepth} + \PrincipalPointColumn\), \(\PixelRowCoordinate \sim \VerticalFocalLength \frac{\CameraFrameVerticalCoordinate}{\CameraFrameDepth} + \PrincipalPointRow\)), italic as scalars; the homogeneous image point is \(\HomogeneousPixelCoordinates = [\PixelColumnCoordinate, \PixelRowCoordinate, 1]^\top\), never bold \(\Glyph{\mathbf{u}}\).


\(\ExposureDuration\)
Exposure Duration
\(\text{ms}\)
Integration time of one camera frame; the frame’s timestamp belongs at its midpoint, \(\ExposureDuration/2\) after exposure starts.


\(\BeliefInvalidationHorizon\)
Belief Invalidation Horizon
\(\text{ms}\)
Time since the last supporting evidence after which a belief can no longer be shown to lie inside its task tolerance; a belief expires at \(\TimeInstant_0 + \BeliefInvalidationHorizon\).


\(\FreeSpaceDepth\)
Free-Space Depth
\(\text{m}\)
Distance from a hull’s surface to the nearest cell that is occupied, unknown, or expired, read from an ESDF built with all three treated as obstacles; the budget motion may spend there (Volumetric metric maps and distance fields).


\(\RollingShutterRowReadout\)
Rolling Shutter Row Readout
\(\MicroUnitPrefix\text{s}\)
Exposure time delta between adjacent CMOS sensor scanlines; row \(\SensorRowIndex\) starts at \(\TimeInstant(\SensorRowIndex) = \FrameExposureStartTime + \SensorRowIndex\,\RollingShutterRowReadout\).


\(\RollingShutterDistortion(\SensorRowIndex)\)
Rolling Shutter Distortion
\(\text{m}\)
Kinematic skew displacement \(\RollingShutterDistortion = \Velocity \cdot \SensorRowIndex \cdot \RollingShutterRowReadout\) induced by high-velocity platform motion.


\(\Glyph{\text{tsdf}}(\VoxelCenterPosition)\)
Truncated Signed Distance
\([-1, +1]\)
Normalized volumetric distance \(\Glyph{\text{tsdf}}(\VoxelCenterPosition) = \text{clamp}(\Glyph{d}(\VoxelCenterPosition)/\TsdfTruncationBand, -1, 1)\) of the voxel centered at \(\VoxelCenterPosition\) to the nearest surface.


\(\TsdfTruncationBand\)
TSDF Truncation Band
\(\text{m}\)
Metric thickness of the spatial surface interface band stored in voxel memory.


\(\TsdfAccumulatedDistance_t(\VoxelCenterPosition), \TsdfAccumulatedWeight_t(\VoxelCenterPosition)\)
TSDF Accumulated Volume
Mixed
Running weighted signed distance and accumulated visibility weight at the voxel centered at \(\VoxelCenterPosition\).


\(\InitialTrackingError, \PositionErrorCeiling\)
Initial and Ceiling Error
\(\text{m}\)
Position error of an estimate when its evidence is fresh, and the largest error the task tolerates; \(\Glyph{E}_0\) and \(\Glyph{E_{\max}}\) stay energies.


\(\PositionalTaskTolerance\)
Positional Task Tolerance
\(\text{m}\)
Radius within which a target estimate must lie for the task to succeed; paired with the orientation tolerance \(\OrientationTolerance\).


\(\GoalSet\)
Geometric Goal Set
Subset of \(\SpecialEuclideanGroup\)
Admissible terminal poses within the positional and angular tolerances of the task; the spatial component of an intent lease \(\IntentLease\).


\(\TargetTravelDistance\)
Distance to Target
\(\text{m}\)
Straight-line distance from the measured end-effector position to the admitted target, \(\lVert \TargetPosition - \CartesianPosition_0 \rVert\), in the intent-lease reachability test; distinct from the hidden width \(\HiddenDimension\).


\(\AttitudeError\)
Attitude Error
\(\text{rad}\)
Angular error in an estimated attitude, which leaks gravity into the horizontal acceleration.


\(\AzimuthAngle\)
Azimuth Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Angle of a direction measured in the horizontal plane about the vertical axis; the book may state values in degrees.


\(\BaseCameraTransform\)
Base-to-Camera Transform
Matrix
Rigid transform mapping camera coordinates into the robot base frame.


\(\BodyFramePoint\)
Body-Frame Point
\(\text{m}\)
Position of a perceived point expressed in the robot body frame, the camera-frame point carried through the extrinsics.


\(\BodyFramePointCovariance\)
Body-Frame Point Covariance
\(\text{m}^2\)
Covariance of a perceived point’s position error in the robot body frame, the spatial covariance an observation contract carries; rotated camera-frame covariance plus the extrinsic term, not the covariance of a state estimator.


\(\CameraExtrinsicRotation\)
Camera Extrinsic Rotation
Dimensionless
Rotation part of a camera’s extrinsic calibration, taking camera-frame vectors into the body frame; the rotation block of \(\CameraExtrinsicTransform\).


\(\CameraExtrinsicTransform\)
Camera Extrinsic Transform
Matrix
Rigid transform of a camera’s extrinsic calibration, mapping camera-frame coordinates into the body frame; mixed rotation and translation blocks.


\(\CameraFramePointCovariance\)
Camera-Frame Point Covariance
\(\text{m}^2\)
Covariance of a point’s position error in the camera’s optical frame, after unprojection of its pixel and depth measurement; rotated into the body frame by \(\CameraExtrinsicRotation\).


\(\CartesianXCoordinate\)
Cartesian X Coordinate
\(\text{m}\)
First Cartesian component of a three-dimensional position.


\(\CartesianYCoordinate\)
Cartesian Y Coordinate
\(\text{m}\)
Second Cartesian component of a three-dimensional position.


\(\CartesianZCoordinate\)
Cartesian Z Coordinate
\(\text{m}\)
Third Cartesian component of a three-dimensional position.


\(\ClearanceInset\)
Clearance Inset
\(\text{m}\)
Separation a consumer holds between an estimated obstacle position and the machine’s envelope so the true obstacle stays the required clearance away, except with a stated tail probability; a field of the observation contract.


\(\DepthStandardDeviation\)
Depth Standard Deviation
\(\text{m}\)
Standard deviation of the depth a stereo or range sensor reports for one point; for stereo it grows with the square of the range.


\(\DisparityStandardDeviation\)
Disparity Standard Deviation
pixels
Standard deviation of the disparity a stereo matcher measures; it feeds the stereo depth term \(\DepthStandardDeviation\).


\(\ElevationAngle\)
Elevation Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Angle of a direction above the horizontal plane; not the encoder parameters of a variational autoencoder, which render the same glyph.


\(\ExtrinsicCalibrationCovariance\)
Extrinsic Calibration Covariance
\(\text{m}^2\)
Covariance of a sensor’s calibrated mounting extrinsic.


\(\ExtrinsicMisalignmentAngle\)
Extrinsic Misalignment Angle
\(\text{rad}\)
Angular error of a sensor’s extrinsic calibration relative to its true mounting.


\(\FocalLength\)
Focal Length
pixels
Focal length of a pinhole camera in pixels, the scale from normalized image coordinates to pixels; a rectified pair shares one value.


\(\HorizontalFocalLength\)
Horizontal Focal Length
pixels
Camera focal length in pixels along the horizontal image axis, one entry of the intrinsics.


\(\FrameExposureStartTime\)
Frame Exposure Start Time
\(\text{s}\)
Instant at which the first row of a rolling-shutter frame begins its exposure.


\(\FrameReadoutTime\)
Frame Readout Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time a camera takes to read its pixels out after exposure.


\(\EvidenceCaptureInstant\)
Evidence Capture Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant, on a monotonic clock, at which the sensor evidence behind an observation or proposal was captured; observation age and proposal validity are measured from it.


\(\EvidenceEpoch\)
Evidence Epoch
\(\text{s}\)
Capture instant of the most recent measurement that constrained a stored belief; republishing or predicting never advances it.


\(\FreshEvidenceTime\)
Fresh Evidence Time
\(\text{s}\)
Capture time of the fresh physical evidence that renews a belief’s evidence epoch \(\EvidenceEpoch\).


\(\CurrentTime\)
Current Time
\(\text{s}\)
Wall-clock time at which a consumer evaluates a stored record; evidence age is the current time minus \(\EvidenceEpoch\).


\(\DispatchObservationAge\)
Dispatch Observation Age
\(\text{s}\)
Elapsed time from the sensor exposure midpoint to dispatch of the processed observation. Current consumer evidence age additionally includes elapsed time after dispatch.


\(\FreeConfigurationSpace\)
Free Configuration Space
Set
Configurations at which the robot touches no obstacle, the configuration space minus the obstacle set.


\(\InverseDepth\)
Inverse Depth
\(\text{1/m}\)
Reciprocal of a point’s depth along the optical axis, the parameterization that lets a landmark at infinity enter an estimator at zero; linear in disparity.


\(\ObstacleSeparationDistance\)
Obstacle Separation Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Distance between the machine and the nearest obstacle or boundary at a given time, the signal a clearance predicate scores; written as a function of time.


\(\OccupancyLogOdds\)
Occupancy Log-Odds
Dimensionless
Natural logarithm of the odds of a voxel’s occupancy probability, the quantity an occupancy map stores per cell; indexed by step, with the prior at step zero.


\(\MeasuredTrackedPosition\)
Measured Tracked Position
\(\text{m}\)
Measured Cartesian position of the tracked point, which the tracking error compares against the reference.


\(\LastMeasurementTime\)
Last Measurement Time
\(\text{s}\)
Capture time of the most recent measurement that updated a track or map cell.


\(\InitialVelocityStandardDeviation\)
Initial Velocity Standard Deviation
\(\text{m/s}\)
Standard deviation of the velocity error of an estimate, here at the onset of occlusion.


\(\PixelStandardDeviation\)
Pixel Standard Deviation
Pixels
Standard deviation of a measured image position, in pixels; the image-plane noise that propagates into depth and position error.


\(\PrincipalPointColumn\)
Principal Point Column
Pixels
Horizontal pixel coordinate of the principal point, where the optical axis meets the image.


\(\PrincipalPointRow\)
Principal Point Row
Pixels
Vertical pixel coordinate of the principal point, where the optical axis meets the image.


\(\StereoBaseline\)
Stereo Baseline
\(\text{m}\)
Distance between the optical centers of a stereo camera pair; depth is focal length times baseline over disparity.


\(\StereoDisparity\)
Stereo Disparity
Pixels
Horizontal pixel offset between the images of one scene point in the two views of a rectified stereo pair; not a travel distance or a sightline range, which share the glyph.


\(\TargetRange\)
Target Range
\(\text{m}\)
Distance from a camera to the target it observes, measured along the viewing direction; stereo depth error grows with its square.


\(\TargetPosition\)
Target Position
\(\text{m}\)
Position of the target an end effector is commanded toward, in the robot base frame; a decorated form of the Cartesian position.


\(\PositionErrorBound\)
Position Error Bound
\(\text{m}\)
Worst-case position error of a target estimate as a function of the time elapsed since its evidence was captured; it grows while the target is occluded.


\(\PositionErrorEnvelope\)
Position Error Envelope
\(\text{m}\)
Conservative bound on the position error of a target estimate along one coordinate axis of the base frame; written with the axis index.


\(\RangeObservation\)
Range Observation
Record
One range observation a sensor returns at a time step; indexed by step, with the history as the sequence of them.


\(\SpatialMemoryMap\)
Spatial Memory Map
Set
Occupancy map in spatial memory that stores the obstacle geometry around the machine; not a decision-process tuple.


\(\TransformRotationBlock\)
Transform Rotation Block
Matrix
Rotation block of the homogeneous transform from frame B to frame A, its upper-left three-by-three part.


\(\TransformTranslationBlock\)
Transform Translation Block
\(\text{m}\)
Translation block of the homogeneous transform from frame B to frame A, the position of the origin of frame B expressed in frame A.


\(\UnprojectionJacobian\)
Unprojection Jacobian
Mixed
Jacobian of a camera-frame point with respect to its pixel coordinates and depth; it carries measurement covariance into Cartesian covariance. Not the manipulator Jacobian \(\ManipulatorJacobian\).


\(\VerticalFocalLength\)
Vertical Focal Length
Pixels
Camera focal length expressed in pixels along the vertical image axis.


\(\WorldBodyTransform\)
World-from-Body Transform
Matrix
Rigid transform giving the pose of the vehicle body frame in the world frame; it maps body coordinates into world coordinates.


\(\WorldFramePoint\)
World-Frame Point
\(\text{m}\)
Position of an observed point expressed in the world frame; compare \(\CameraFramePoint\), the same point in the camera frame.


\(\PerceptionDepthCovariance\)
Perception Depth Covariance
\(\text{m}^2\)
Covariance of the three-dimensional position error of a point lifted from stereo, lidar, or depth data; a matrix, not the scalar depth variance.


\(\VacuumLightSpeed\)
Speed of Light in Vacuum
\(\text{m/s}\)
About \(3 \times 10^8\) m/s, the upper limit on how fast a signal crosses a chip or link; on-chip wires carry signals at a fraction of it.

title: Notation
text:
The control symbols follow state-space convention. A plant has a state, an input, and a measured output; an observer estimates the state from that output; and a safety filter, such as a control barrier function solved as a quadratic program, edits the input before it reaches the actuators.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\StateSpaceSystemMatrix, \StateSpaceInputMatrix\)
Linear State-Space Matrices
Matrix
Continuous LTI plant: \(\PlantStateRate = \StateSpaceSystemMatrix\MechanicalPlantState + \StateSpaceInputMatrix\ControlInput + \ProcessNoiseVector\), observed output \(\MeasurementVector = \MeasurementMatrix\MechanicalPlantState + \MeasurementNoiseVector\) through the measurement map \(\MeasurementMatrix\) below.


\(\ProcessNoiseVector(\TimeInstant), \MeasurementNoiseVector(\TimeInstant)\)
Process and Measurement Noise
Vector
Zero-mean Gaussian noise vectors with covariance matrices \(\ProcessNoiseCovariance \succeq 0\) and \(\MeasurementNoiseCovariance \succ 0\); bold \(\DirectionalCosineMatrix\) is reserved for rotation.


\(\StateTransitionMatrix, \MeasurementMatrix\)
Transition and Measurement Maps
Matrix
Discrete state transition \(\PredictedStateEstimate = \StateTransitionMatrix\PreviousUpdatedStateEstimate\) and measurement map \(\MeasurementVector_k = \MeasurementMatrix\MechanicalPlantState_k + \MeasurementNoiseVector\) of a Kalman filter.


\(\KalmanGain_{k}\)
Kalman Gain
Matrix
Weight on the innovation \(\MeasurementInnovation_k = \MeasurementVector_k - \MeasurementMatrix\PredictedStateEstimate\) in the update step; bold \(\CameraIntrinsicCalibrationMatrix\) is reserved for camera intrinsics.


\(\EstimationErrorCovariance \in \mathbb{R}^{\StateDimension \times \StateDimension}\)
Estimation Error Covariance
Matrix
Symmetric positive-definite matrix \(\mathbb{E}[(\MechanicalPlantState - \StateEstimate)(\MechanicalPlantState - \StateEstimate)^\top]\) (\(\EstimationErrorCovariance(\TimeInstant)\) continuous, \(\UpdatedErrorCovariance\) discrete) evolving via matrix Riccati equation; \(\Glyph{\mathbf{P}_{\text{est}}}\) where an LQR cost matrix is also in scope.


\(\ObservabilityMatrix, \NonlinearObservationSpace\)
Observability Matrices
Matrix
Kalman observability matrix \([\MeasurementMatrix^\top, (\MeasurementMatrix\StateSpaceSystemMatrix)^\top, \dots]^\top\) and nonlinear Lie matrix \([\DerivativeOperator\NonlinearOutputFunction, d\DriftLieDerivativeOperator\NonlinearOutputFunction, \dots]^\top\); calligraphic \(\mathcal{O}(\cdot)\) stays asymptotic cost. The dual controllability matrix is \(\ControllabilityMatrix\).


\(\ControllabilityMatrix\)
Controllability Matrix
Mixed
Kalman block matrix formed from the input matrix and its products with powers of the system matrix; full row rank characterizes unconstrained LTI controllability.


\(\SafetyBoundaryManifold\)
Safety Boundary Manifold
Boundary
Zero level set \(\{\MechanicalPlantState \mid \BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) = 0\}\), the boundary of the safe set \(\ForwardInvariantSafeSet\), separating nominal operation from irreversible hazard.


\(\BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState), \BarrierFunction\)
Control Barrier Function (CBF)
Scalar
Continuously differentiable function whose 0-superlevel set is the safe set \(\ForwardInvariantSafeSet\). Written \(\BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState)\) on the plant state, and as the function head \(\BarrierFunction\) when it takes other arguments or is differentiated (\(\BarrierFunctionRate\), \(\DriftLieDerivativeOperator \BarrierFunction\), \(\BarrierFunction(\Glyph{\theta_{\text{clear}}}, \JointAngularSpeed)\)).


\(\ForwardInvariantSafeSet \subset \mathbb{R}^{2\GeneralizedCoordinateCount}\)
Forward-Invariant Safe Set
Set
Superlevel set \(\ForwardInvariantSafeSet = \{\MechanicalPlantState \mid \BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) \ge 0\}\) of plant states where safety invariants are strictly maintained; a qualifier names a variant (\(\Glyph{\ForwardinvariantSafeSet}_{\text{contact}}\), \(\Glyph{\ForwardinvariantSafeSet}_{\text{discrete}}\)).


\(\ControlAffineDriftField(\MechanicalPlantState), \ControlAffineInputField(\MechanicalPlantState)\)
Control-Affine Drift and Input Fields
Vector, Matrix
The control-affine model \(\PlantStateRate = \ControlAffineDriftField(\MechanicalPlantState) + \ControlAffineInputField(\MechanicalPlantState)\ControlInput\) of barrier analysis; these letters hold only inside that model, where the gravity torque \(\GravitationalTorqueVector(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\) and contact forces \(\ContactPointForce_{k}\) do not appear.


\(\LieDerivativeAlongDrift(\MechanicalPlantState)\)
Lie Derivative along Drift
Barrier units/s
Directional gradient derivative \(\nabla \BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) \ControlAffineDriftField(\MechanicalPlantState)\) along unforced plant dynamics; its units are those of the barrier divided by time.


\(\LieDerivativeAlongControl(\MechanicalPlantState)\)
Lie Derivative along Control
Vector
Directional control effectiveness gradient \(\nabla \BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) \ControlAffineInputField(\MechanicalPlantState)\).


\(\BarrierRelativeDegree\)
Barrier Relative Degree
Integer
Number of differentiations required before control input \(\ControlInput\) appears (\(\InputLieDerivativeOperator \DriftLieDerivativeOperator^{\BarrierRelativeDegree-1} \BarrierFunction \neq 0\)).


\(\KineticInsetBarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState)\)
Kinetic Inset Barrier Function
Scalar
Relative-degree-1 barrier: \(\KineticInsetBarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) = \BarrierFunction(\MechanicalPlantState) - \BodySpeed^2 / (2 \CredibleBrakingDeceleration)\) incorporating stopping distance.


\(\ClassKFunction(\cdot), \ClassKFunction\)
Class-\(\ClassKFunctionSet\) Rate Function
Scalar function
Extended class-\(\ClassKFunctionSet\) function in the barrier condition \(\BarrierFunctionRate \ge -\ClassKFunction(\BarrierFunction)\), written as the function head \(\ClassKFunction\) when applied; the book uses the linear choice \(\ClassKFunction(\BarrierFunction) = \LinearBarrierDecayRate \BarrierFunction\).


\(\LinearBarrierDecayRate\)
Linear Barrier Decay Rate
\(\text{s}^{-1}\)
Coefficient of the linear class-\(\ClassKFunctionSet\) choice, \(\BarrierFunctionRate + \LinearBarrierDecayRate \BarrierFunction \ge 0\); bare \(\DiscountFactor\) is the reinforcement-learning discount factor.


\(\NominalControlCommand \in \AdmissibleControlSet\)
Nominal Control Command
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\) / \(\text{rad}\)
Unverified control candidate proposed across the proposal boundary by the learned policy.


\(\CertifiedControlAction \in \AdmissibleControlSet\)
Certified Control Action
\(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\) / \(\text{rad}\)
Privileged, safety-filtered control command resolved by the real-time active-set CBF-QP.


\(\ReferencePosition\)
Reference Position
\(\text{m}\)
Commanded Cartesian position reference the plant tracks, \(\ReferencePosition(\TimeInstant)\); the feedback tracker bounds the tracked point’s position error by \(\lVert \CartesianPosition(\TimeInstant) - \ReferencePosition(\TimeInstant) \rVert \le \TrackingErrorBound\), with both positions expressed in the same frame. Whole-body clearance requires a declared output map or metric that bounds swept-volume displacement. Elsewhere bold \(\Glyph{\mathbf{r}}\) is local (a moment arm, ellipsoid semi-axes).


\(\BumplessTransferBlend(\BumplessTransferProgress)\)
Bumpless Transfer Blend
\([0, 1]\)
\(\Glyph{C}^2\) quintic polynomial \(6\BumplessTransferProgress^5 - 15\BumplessTransferProgress^4 + 10\BumplessTransferProgress^3\) of normalized time \(\BumplessTransferProgress \in [0, 1]\), ramping between prior and candidate controllers.


\(\BumplessTransferBlendSlope\)
Blend slope
Dimensionless
Derivative of the bumpless-transfer blend weight \(\BumplessTransferBlend\) with respect to normalized progress.


\(\BlendingTransitionWindow\)
Blending Transition Window
\(\text{s}\)
Duration of bumpless transfer; for two fixed, latched acceleration commands, bounded by \(\Glyph{\tau_{\text{blend}, \min}} = 1.875 \lVert \FiniteChange \ControlInput \rVert / \JerkLimit\). Torque or position commands require their own compatible command-rate bounds.


\(\PidProportionalGain, \PidDerivativeGain, \PidIntegralGain\)
PID / Feedback Gains
Mixed
Proportional, derivative, and integral gains for joint-level or operational-space error stabilization.


\(\LqrFeedbackGain, \LqrStateWeightMatrix, \LqrControlWeightMatrix\)
LQR Gain and Weights
Matrix
State-feedback gain \(\CertifiedControlAction = -\LqrFeedbackGain\MechanicalPlantState\) and the state and control weights of the quadratic cost; the subscripts keep them distinct from intrinsics, process noise, and rotation.


\(\MpcPredictionHorizon\)
MPC Prediction Horizon
Control steps
Number of predicted discrete control steps in the finite-horizon MPC formulation; distinct from physical-trial count and learned action-chunk horizon.


\(\VirtualDampingMatrix, \Glyph{\mathbf{K}_{\text{virt}}}\)
Virtual Damping & Stiffness Matrices
Matrix
Target compliance matrices in impedance control: \(\Glyph{\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{safe}}} = -\VirtualDampingMatrix \GeneralizedVelocities - \Glyph{\mathbf{K}_{\text{virt}}} \FiniteChange\GeneralizedCoordinates + \GravitationalTorqueVector(\GeneralizedCoordinates)\).


\(\AccelerationNoiseSpectralDensity\)
Acceleration Noise Spectral Density
\(\text{m}^2/\text{s}^3\)
Continuous power spectral density of the zero-mean white acceleration noise per axis in a constant-velocity motion model; sets how fast the predicted position uncertainty grows.


\(\AdmissibleDisturbanceSet\)
Admissible Disturbance Set
Set
Set of disturbance values a falsification search may inject; the search is bounded to it.


\(\AdmittedControlCommand\)
Admitted Control Command
Per interface
Control command the permission path applies to the actuators after admitting, clipping, or replacing a policy proposal; indexed by step. Not \(\NominalControlCommand\) (before the filter) or \(\CertifiedControlAction\) (the filter’s projection).


\(\AngularFrequency\)
