Angular Frequency
\(\text{rad/s}\)
Frequency of a sinusoidal signal, the free variable of a frequency response; evaluated at the crossover frequency when a delay’s phase lag is charged to the phase margin.


\(\BackwardEulerTransitionMatrix\)
Backward Euler Transition Matrix
Matrix
Discrete-time transition matrix that backward (implicit) Euler integration produces, the inverse of the identity minus the system matrix times the step; unconditionally stable but numerically dissipative.


\(\BarrierConstraintBound\)
Barrier Constraint Bound
Varies
Bound on the right side of one affine control-barrier constraint, one entry of \(\Glyph{\mathbf{b}_{\text{cbf}}}\); its unit follows the barrier function rate.


\(\BarrierConstraintNormal\)
Barrier Constraint Normal
Varies
Normal vector of a single affine control-barrier constraint on the control input, equal to \(-\LieDerivativeAlongControl\) transposed; one row of \(\Glyph{\mathbf{A}_{\text{cbf}}}\).


\(\BarrierFunctionRate\)
Barrier Function Rate
\(\text{m/s}\)
Time derivative of the control barrier function along the closed-loop dynamics, the rate in the barrier condition; a dot is not an allowed decoration on \(\BarrierFunction\), so it has its own entry.


\(\BarrierProjectionMultiplier\)
Barrier Projection Multiplier
Varies
Lagrange multiplier of the barrier half-space constraint in the CBF-QP projection; starred at the optimum, where it is zero when the nominal command is already safe.


\(\BeliefErrorBound\)
Belief Error Bound
Varies
Upper bound on the discrepancy between a stored belief and the true state after a given elapsed time without new evidence; the unit is that of the stored quantity (meters for a position, radians for an angle).


\(\BumplessTransferStartInstant\)
Bumpless Transfer Start Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant at which a bumpless-transfer blend begins, the zero of its normalized progress; other chapters use the same letters for exposure or sweep starts, different quantities.


\(\ChannelCommand\)
Channel Command
Varies
Scalar command of one actuator channel, such as the base acceleration or one joint torque; the unit is the channel’s command unit. Scalar per-channel form of \(\ControlCommand\).


\(\ClassKFunctionSet\)
Class-K Function Set
Set
Class of continuous strictly increasing functions that are zero at zero; named in “extended class-K function.”


\(\ControlCommand\)
Control Command
Per interface
Control command vector sent toward the actuators, whatever its source or stage; indices name instances. The stages are \(\NominalControlCommand\) and \(\CertifiedControlAction\).


\(\ControlInput\)
Control Input
Per interface
Control input applied to the plant, the command a controller or safety filter sends to the actuators; units depend on the command interface (torques, setpoints).


\(\ControlInputDimension\)
Control Input Dimension
Count
Number of components of the control input vector; not the mass \(\Mass\).


\(\ControlInputLowerLimit\)
Control Input Lower Limit
Per interface
Per-component lower limit of the control input the actuators can deliver.


\(\ControlInputSet\)
Control Input Set
Set
Set of control inputs the controller may choose from, a subset of the input space; the actuator box and the barrier-feasible subset are narrower sets inside it.


\(\ControlInputUpperLimit\)
Control Input Upper Limit
Vector
Per-component upper limit of the control input the actuators can deliver.


\(\ControlStepIndex\)
Control Step Index
Dimensionless
Position of one discrete control step, or setpoint, in a robot’s control timeline; a subscript on per-step quantities, bare in expressions such as a clipped next step.


\(\DerivativeGainMatrix\)
Derivative Gain Matrix
Matrix
Derivative feedback gains acting on the tracking error rate in joint-space PD or PID control; its diagonal entries are the per-joint derivative gains.


\(\DifferentiabilityClass\)
Differentiability Class
Set
Functions whose derivatives up to the order written as the superscript exist and are continuous; \(\DifferentiabilityClass^2\) means continuous position, velocity, and acceleration of a blended trajectory.


\(\DiscretePlantDynamics\)
Discrete Plant Dynamics
Function
Discrete-time map from the current state and applied command to the next state; the deterministic counterpart of the plant’s transition kernel.


\(\DriftLieDerivativeOperator\)
Drift Lie Derivative Operator
Operator
Rate of change of a scalar function of the state under the unforced dynamics; it is applied repeatedly for higher-order derivatives.


\(\DriftSpeedBound\)
Drift Speed Bound
\(\text{m/s}\)
Bound on the unobserved speed at which a target drifts relative to its last measured position; not the bound on the state-estimate drift, \(\DriftVelocityBound\).


\(\DriftVelocityBound\)
Drift Velocity Bound
\(\text{m/s}\)
Bound on the unmodeled velocity at which an unobserved estimate drifts from the true state.


\(\ConveyorSpeedBound\)
Conveyor Speed Bound
\(\text{m/s}\)
Largest speed at which the takeaway conveyor carries a target; the bound used when sizing a catch window, not the belt speed \(\ConveyorSpeed\) of a single pick.


\(\EstimatedPlantState\)
Estimated Plant State
Mixed
Estimate of the mechanical plant state reconstructed from sensor observations; its error covariance is a separate symbol.


\(\EstimatedPosition\)
Estimated Position
\(\text{m}\)
Position of a point that a filter propagates under its nominal model.


\(\EstimatedVelocity\)
Estimated Velocity
\(\text{m/s}\)
Velocity of a body that a filter propagates under its nominal model.


\(\FiniteTimeHorizon\)
Finite Time Horizon
\(\text{s}\)
Length of the finite window from time zero to the horizon over which an optimization, rollout, test, or temporal-logic operator is evaluated; not the wall-clock time to complete a unit of work.


\(\ForwardEulerTransitionMatrix\)
Forward Euler Transition Matrix
Matrix
Discrete-time transition matrix that forward Euler integration produces, identity plus the system matrix times the step; its spectral radius exceeds one for an undamped oscillator at any step size.


\(\HermiteBasisFunction\)
Hermite Basis Function
Function
Cubic Hermite basis polynomial that weights an endpoint position or velocity in spline interpolation; indexed by two digits.


\(\ImaginaryUnit\)
Imaginary Unit
Dimensionless
Square root of minus one, written \(\ImaginaryUnit\) by the engineering convention rather than \(\Glyph{i}\).


\(\InductiveVoltage\)
Inductive Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Voltage across a coil, the inductance times the rate of change of its current.


\(\InequalityConstraintFunction\)
Inequality Constraint Function
Varies
Constraint function of an optimization problem, whose nonpositive values define the feasible set; it appears in the interior-point barrier.


\(\InputLieDerivativeOperator\)
Input Lie Derivative Operator
Operator
Lie derivative along the input matrix field, mapping a scalar function of the state to its sensitivity to the control input.


\(\IntegrationTimeInstant\)
Integration Time Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Time instant running over an integration interval, the dummy variable when the interval ends at the time \(\TimeInstant\); it keeps the integrand’s time distinct from the upper limit.


\(\IntegrationDummyTime\)
Integration Dummy Time
\(\text{s}\)
Dummy time variable of integration inside a time integral, distinct from its limits; a primed time would be a decorated quantity, so this entry names the bound variable.


\(\LaplaceVariable\)
Laplace Variable
\(\text{1/s}\)
Complex frequency variable of the Laplace transform, standing for differentiation in time; read as the imaginary unit times the angular frequency for sinusoidal motion.


\(\LargestEigenvalue\)
Largest Eigenvalue
Varies
Largest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix, applied to that matrix; its unit is that of the matrix entries.


\(\LqrCostToGoMatrix\)
LQR Cost-to-Go Matrix
Varies
Symmetric solution of the regulator algebraic Riccati equation (the discrete one in discrete-time LQR), whose quadratic form is the optimal LQR cost-to-go; shares its glyph with the estimation error covariance.


\(\MpcControlSequence\)
MPC Control Sequence
Varies
Sequence of control inputs over a model-predictive-control horizon, one per step, that the optimizer chooses; only the first is applied before the next re-solve.


\(\NonlinearOutputFunction\)
Nonlinear Output Function
Varies
Output function of a nonlinear state-space model, mapping the state to the measurement vector \(\MeasurementVector\); not the barrier function nor the bias forces of the floating-base equations.


\(\OpenLoopTransferFunction\)
Open-Loop Transfer Function
Dimensionless
Open-loop transfer function of a feedback loop, evaluated along the imaginary axis for frequency response; never the loss.


\(\PidProportionalGainMatrix\)
PID Proportional Gain Matrix
Varies
Proportional gain matrix of multi-joint PD or PID feedback, the stiffness acting on the position error.


\(\MeasurementVector\)
Measurement Vector
Varies
Measurement vector a sensor or detector reports at one step.


\(\MeasurementInnovation\)
Measurement Innovation
Varies
Difference between a measurement and the measurement the predicted state implies; its normalized square is the NIS.


\(\MeasurementNoiseCovariance\)
Measurement Noise Covariance
Varies
Covariance of the noise on a sensor measurement vector, such as a pixel position with depth or a Kalman filter measurement; units are those of the measurement squared.


\(\PathDelayAsymmetry\)
Path Delay Asymmetry
\(\text{s}\)
Difference between the forward and reverse one-way delays of a clock-synchronization exchange, which biases the estimated clock offset by half its value; two-way time transfer assumes it is zero.


\(\PredictedStateEstimate\)
Predicted State Estimate
Vector
State estimate at step \(\Glyph{k}\) predicted from measurements through the previous step, before the measurement update; the step index is part of the symbol.


\(\PredictedErrorCovariance\)
Predicted Error Covariance
Matrix
Error covariance at step \(\Glyph{k}\) predicted from measurements through the previous step, before the update; the conditioned form of the estimation error covariance.


\(\PreviousUpdatedStateEstimate\)
Previous Updated State Estimate
Vector
State estimate at the previous step after that step’s update, the input to the next prediction.


\(\PreviousUpdatedErrorCovariance\)
Previous Updated Error Covariance
Matrix
Error covariance at the previous step after that step’s update, the input to the next prediction.


\(\ProcessNoiseCovariance\)
Process Noise Covariance
Matrix
Covariance of the process noise vector; the predict step adds it to the error covariance.


\(\StateEstimate\)
State Estimate
Vector
Estimate of the state vector that a recursive estimator maintains; conditioned forms with the step index baked in have their own symbols.


\(\ProportionalGainMatrix\)
Proportional Gain Matrix
Matrix
Matrix of proportional feedback gains acting on the tracking error vector in joint-space PD or PID control; its diagonal entries are the per-joint proportional gains, and it is not the camera calibration matrix.


\(\SafeControlSet\)
Safe Control Set
Set
Set of control inputs that satisfy every active barrier constraint and the actuator limits at the current state; it is empty when saturation leaves no command that keeps the barrier condition, which selects a fallback.


\(\SafeStateConstraintSet\)
Safe State Constraint Set
Set
Set of plant states that satisfy the state constraints of a model predictive control problem, such as joint limits and obstacle margins; polyhedral, and not the barrier safe set.


\(\SafeSeparationDistance\)
Safe Separation Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Smallest separation from an obstacle that a clearance requirement allows.


\(\SignalTrajectory\)
Signal Trajectory
Function
Trajectory of a system’s real-valued signals over continuous time, the trace a temporal logic formula is evaluated on; two trajectories are told apart by subscripts.


\(\StlFormula\)
Signal Temporal Logic Formula
Record
Signal temporal logic formula a signal must satisfy, such as a safety invariant or a reachability deadline; subscripts index subformulas.


\(\StlPredicateFunction\)
Signal Temporal Logic Predicate Function
Function
Real-valued function of a signal whose sign decides an atomic temporal-logic predicate; its unit is the physical unit of that predicate’s margin, and it is indexed per predicate.


\(\StlRobustness\)
Signal Temporal Logic Robustness
Function
Signed margin by which a signal satisfies (positive) or violates (negative) a temporal logic formula at a time; it carries the units of the atomic predicates when they agree and is dimensionless after a declared normalization. Not a correlation coefficient.


\(\SmallChange\)
Small Change
Operator
Small change, increment or error in the quantity it prefixes; the companion of the finite change for first-order changes.


\(\SmallPerturbation\)
Small Perturbation
Operator
Small change or error in the quantity it prefixes, treated to first order, as in a perturbation of a signal or a time; not a labeled localization bound that also renders \(\Glyph{\delta}\).


\(\PolynomialTrajectoryCoefficient\)
Polynomial Trajectory Coefficient
Varies
Coefficient of one power of time in a polynomial joint trajectory segment, indexed by the power it multiplies; its unit is the joint unit divided by seconds to that power, and it is not an acceleration.


\(\SetpointSampleIndex\)
Setpoint Sample Index
Index
Position of one discrete setpoint sample in a sampled trajectory.


\(\SetpointStepInterval\)
Setpoint Step Interval
\(\text{s}\)
Time between consecutive setpoints of an action chunk, the spacing at which the controller consumes them; the reciprocal of the action execution rate.


\(\StateSpaceDimension\)
State Space Dimension
Dimensionless
Number of continuous coordinates in the task-relevant state.


\(\StopCompletionInstant\)
Stop Completion Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant, on the permission clock, at which the matched stop of an admitted trajectory record reaches rest; the commitment instant plus the stopping duration.


\(\StoppingDeadline\)
Stopping Deadline
\(\text{s}\)
Latest instant at which authority can be revoked and a worst-case stop still ends within the verified clearance.


\(\PolicyLipschitzBound\)
Policy Lipschitz Bound
Varies
Lipschitz bound of a learned policy over a stated operating domain, the largest ratio of action change to state change; it gives no guarantee unless established for that domain, and times the sensor error bound it bounds the action error.


\(\TaskToleranceSemiAxes\)
Task Tolerance Semi-Axes
\(\text{m}\)
Principal semi-axes of the ellipsoid within which terminal position error must lie; the vector of \(\TaskToleranceSemiAxis\) values.


\(\TaskToleranceSemiAxis\)
Task Tolerance Semi-Axis
\(\text{m}\)
Semi-axis of the task tolerance ellipsoid along one coordinate axis, written with the axis index.


\(\TerminalInvariantSet\)
Terminal Invariant Set
Set
Plant states from which an invariant fallback control law keeps the system safe indefinitely, the required endpoint of a receding horizon. On an embodied system a validated stop that reaches rest within verified clearance realizes it.


\(\TrackingErrorVector\)
Tracking Error Vector
Vector
Commanded reference state minus measured state of a feedback controller, acted on by \(\ProportionalGainMatrix\). Not the error feedback residual, which shares the glyph.


\(\TrackingErrorRate\)
Tracking Error Rate
Vector
Time derivative of the tracking error vector, the velocity error of a feedback controller; multiplied by \(\DerivativeGainMatrix\) in PD control, so a step in it produces a torque step.


\(\UnitImpulseFunction\)
Unit Impulse Function
\(\text{s}^{-1}\)
Dirac delta, the idealized unit impulse of zero width and unit area; with time as its argument it carries inverse seconds.


\(\UpdatedErrorCovariance\)
Updated Error Covariance
Matrix
Error covariance at a step after incorporating that step’s measurement, the posterior counterpart of \(\EstimationErrorCovariance\).


\(\UpdatedStateEstimate\)
Updated State Estimate
Vector
State estimate at a step after incorporating that step’s measurement, the posterior estimate of a Kalman filter.


\(\DerivativeOperator\)
Derivative Operator
Operator
Differential operator of an ordinary derivative, written over the differential in a Leibniz quotient. Prefer writing the derivative so the \(\Glyph{d}\) sits before a variable.


\(\FiniteChange\)
Finite Change
Operator
Finite change in the quantity it prefixes, between two states, configurations, or points in time. Differs from the increment fused into named entries such as \(\JouleanTemperatureRise\).


\(\PathCoordinate\)
Path Coordinate
Dimensionless
Scalar coordinate along a geometric path, from zero at its start to one at its end, that a timing law maps to time; not a Laplace variable.

title: Notation
text:
Learned policies propose actions rather than issue them. The symbols below cover how those policies are trained and sampled, including diffusion denoising, action chunking, and vision-language-action models, and how their imitation and reinforcement-learning objectives are written.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\Policy\)
Policy
Distribution
Deep policy network parameterized by weights \(\ModelParameters\) (italic), mapping observation tensors to action distributions.


\(\MultimodalObservation_{t}\)
Multimodal Observation
Mixed
Synchronized tokenized sensor packet (RGB images, depth latents, joint encoders, tactile arrays).


\(\CognitivePolicyAction_{t} \in \ActionSpace\)
Cognitive Policy Action
Normalized
Unprivileged action emitted by neural policy \(\Policy\) (normalized joint delta, target pose, or gripper command).


\(\EnsemblingWindowLength\)
Ensembling Window Length
Time steps
Number of overlapping past chunks blended in receding horizon execution (\(\EnsemblingWindowLength \le \ActionChunkHorizon\)).


\(\DecoderEvaluationCount\)
Decoder Evaluation Count
Count
Dependent forward passes of a generative action head per chunk (denoising or ODE-solver steps); distinct from the ensembling window \(\EnsemblingWindowLength\) and the step index \(\DiffusionStepIndex\).


\(\LatentStyleVariable \in \mathbb{R}^{\LatentDimension}\)
Latent Style / State Embedding
Dimensionless
Compressed semantic representation or CVAE latent style variable in ACT policies.


\(\DiffusionCumulativeSchedule_{k}\)
Diffusion Schedule Parameter
\([0, 1]\)
Cumulative noise variance schedule parameter \(\DiffusionCumulativeSchedule_{k} = \prod_{\Glyph{s}=1}^{\DiffusionStepIndex} (1 - \Glyph{\beta}_{\Glyph{s}})\) at diffusion step \(\DiffusionStepIndex\).


\(\DiffusionGaussianNoise \sim \GaussianDistribution(\ZeroVector, \IdentityMatrix)\)
Diffusion Gaussian Noise
Tensor
Standard normal Gaussian noise corrupted onto clean action trajectories.


\(\NoisePredictionNetwork(\MultimodalObservation_{t}, \NoisedActionChunk_t, \DiffusionStepIndex)\)
Noise Prediction Network
Tensor
Neural network predicting added noise in Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM).


\(\NoisedActionChunk\)
Noised Action Chunk
Tensor
Action chunk after \(\DiffusionStepIndex\) forward-diffusion steps, \(\sqrt{\DiffusionCumulativeSchedule_{k}}\,\ActionChunk^0 + \sqrt{1 - \DiffusionCumulativeSchedule_{k}}\,\DiffusionGaussianNoise\); the denoising iterate the reverse process refines.


\(\DiffusionMatchingLoss(\ModelParameters)\)
Diffusion Matching Loss
Scalar
Mean-squared error objective: \(\mathbb{E}[\lVert \DiffusionGaussianNoise - \NoisePredictionNetwork(\MultimodalObservation_{t}, \NoisedActionChunk_t, \DiffusionStepIndex) \rVert^2]\) optimized across denoising steps.


\(\ActVariationalObjective(\ModelParameters, \CvaeEncoderParameters)\)
ACT Variational Objective
Scalar
CVAE objective combining trajectory reconstruction \(\Glyph{\mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}}}\) with latent KL-regularization \(\LatentKlWeight \KlDivergence\).


\(\CvaeRecognitionEncoder(\LatentStyleVariable \mid \MultimodalObservation, \ActionChunk)\)
CVAE Recognition Encoder
Distribution
Variational encoder in Action Chunking with Transformers parameterizing latent distribution \(\GaussianDistribution(\GaussianMeanVector, \GaussianCovarianceMatrix)\); \(\CvaeEncoderParameters\) here is the encoder’s parameter set.


\(\DivergenceInstant\)
Divergence Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Time at which the autonomous policy’s rollout begins to leave its supported states before a takeover; the start of the interval excluded from imitation targets.


\(\TrajectoryDivergenceResidual\)
Trajectory Divergence Residual
\(\text{m}\)
Signed lateral gripper-position error between measured and planned kinematics in the declared fixture frame for the latch example.


\(\DivergenceTolerance\)
Divergence Tolerance
\(\text{m}\)
Positive threshold for the declared trajectory-divergence residual; expressed in that residual’s physical unit.


\(\Reward\)
Reward
Scalar
Per-step reward \(\Reward(\PhysicalWorldState, \CognitivePolicyAction)\) that policy search maximizes; the stage cost of control is its negative. The barrier relative degree \(\BarrierRelativeDegree\) also renders \(\BarrierRelativeDegree\) but appears only in barrier analysis.


\(\ResidualGate\)
Residual Gate
\(\{0, 1\}\)
Deterministic, independently evaluated gate \(\ResidualGate(\PhysicalWorldState)\) that admits a learned residual correction only inside the certified contact region and is zero elsewhere.


\(\TrialCount\)
Trial Count
Trials
Number of physical trials (rollouts) in a learning or evaluation campaign, which sets its wall-clock cost; distinct from the zero-failure trial count \(\Glyph{n}\).


\(\SingleStepImitationError\)
Single-Step Imitation Error
\([0, 1]\)
Bounded probability of an unforced policy error during an individual execution step; bold \(\DiffusionGaussianNoise\) is diffusion noise, the conformal miscoverage rate is \(\ConformalMiscoverageRate\), and other error bounds carry a subscript (\(\TrackingErrorBound\)).


\(\BehaviorCloningHorizon\)
Behavioral-Cloning Horizon
Control steps
Episode length in control steps over which imitation error compounds; not the action-chunk horizon \(\ActionChunkHorizon\), not a duration \(\Glyph{T}\), and not the token sequence length \(\SequenceLength\).


\(\CovariateDriftBound\)
Compounding Covariate-Drift Bound
Task cost
Worst-case excess cost of fixed-archive behavioral cloning, which grows quadratically over a rollout of \(\BehaviorCloningHorizon\) control steps with per-step error \(\SingleStepImitationError\).


\(\VitPatchProjectionWeights, \Glyph{\mathbf{E}_{\text{pos}}}\)
ViT Projection & Positional Bias
Matrix
Convolutional/linear patch projection matrix and spatial coordinate position embedding tensors.


\(\MultimodalFusedTokenStream\)
Multimodal Fused Token Stream
Tensor
Concatenated token sequence \([\VisionTokenEmbeddings, \TextTokenEmbeddings, \ProprioceptiveTokenEmbeddings]\) ingested by embodied transformer backbones.


\(\KvCacheMemory\)
KV-Cache Memory
bytes
Autoregressive key-value cache memory footprint at the embodied batch size \(\BatchSize = 1\) (\(2 \times \LayerCount \times \HiddenDimension \times \SequenceLength \times \ElementStorageSize\) with full multi-head attention); the core’s quantity.


\(\IntentLease\)
Intent Lease
Tuple
\((\GoalSet, [\LeaseAdmissionInstant, \IntentLeaseExpiry], \ContactWrenchCeiling)\): the admitted goal set, its validity interval, and its effort ceilings; it names a target, never a path. Calligraphic \(\LossFunction\) stays the loss.


\(\IntentLeaseExpiry\)
Intent-Lease Expiry
\(\text{s}\)
\(\IntentLeaseExpiry = \min(\TimeInstant_0 + \EvidenceHorizon,\, \LeaseAdmissionInstant + \IntentAdministrativeLease,\, \Glyph{t_{\text{deadline,stop}}})\), where \(\Glyph{t_{\text{deadline,stop}}}\) is the instant by which a stop must begin; see the lease table above.


\(\EvidenceHorizon\)
Evidence Horizon
\(\text{ms}\)
Time for which a target estimate stays within its task tolerance without fresh evidence.


\(\ConformalPredictionSet\)
Conformal Prediction Set
Set
Calibrated set of referent candidates that cannot be excluded at miscoverage rate \(\ConformalMiscoverageRate\); a singleton admits the referent, and a larger set refuses. It shares the glyph of the safe set \(\ForwardInvariantSafeSet\), but the two never appear together.


\(\ConformalMiscoverageRate\)
Conformal Miscoverage Rate
Probability
Allowed marginal probability that the conformal prediction set misses the true referent under the calibration procedure’s exchangeability assumptions; coverage is at least \(1 - \ConformalMiscoverageRate\).


\(\ExternalWait\)
External Wait
Seconds
Time the machine spends waiting for a remote operator’s response during a handover or intervention.


\(\AggregatedSurrogateLoss\)
Aggregated Surrogate Loss
Dimensionless
Best-in-class surrogate imitation loss on the states the learner visited, aggregated over the rounds so far; differs from the error measured on expert-visited states.


\(\AggregationLearnedPolicy\)
Aggregation Learned Policy
Function
Policy trained in one round of corrective dataset aggregation, one of the sequence the bound selects from; carries a round index in the appendix.


\(\ChunkExecutionHorizon\)
Chunk Execution Horizon
Count
Number of actions of each predicted chunk the controller executes before the policy is queried again; at most the chunk horizon.


\(\ChunkStepIndex\)
Chunk Step Index
Index
Position of one step within an action chunk, counted from zero.


\(\ConservativePenaltyWeight\)
Conservative Penalty Weight
Dimensionless
Weight of the conservative penalty that pushes down values of unsupported actions in conservative Q-learning.


\(\ContinuousActionSpace\)
Continuous Action Space
Set
Set of continuous actions a robot policy may emit, a subset of real space of the action dimension.


\(\ContinuousActionVector\)
Continuous Action Vector
Varies
Continuous action vector of the robot’s decision process, written without a step index: the argument of a policy, value function, reward, or action distribution, or an action recorded from a demonstrator. A star marks the demonstrated action; it lives in \(\ContinuousActionSpace\).


\(\CriticActionReturnEstimate\)
Critic Action-Value Estimate
Function
Return a learned critic predicts for a state and an action; the action counterpart of the critic’s state-value estimate.


\(\DecoderPassTime\)
Decoder Pass Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time of one dependent forward pass of a generative action head, one denoising or ODE-solver step; summed over the decoder evaluations in the proposer inference time.


\(\DemonstrationActionDistribution\)
Demonstration Action Distribution
Distribution
Conditional distribution of the actions demonstrators took given an observation, the target a behavioral cloning decoder models; its mean minimizes squared error and can fall between modes (mode averaging).


\(\DemonstrationDataset\)
Demonstration Dataset
Set
Recorded observation-action pairs that an imitation loss averages over.


\(\EmpiricalTimestepAverage\)
Empirical Timestep Average
Operator
Sample average over the timesteps of a batch of rollouts, the estimate of an expectation.


\(\EnsemblingDecayRate\)
Ensembling Decay Rate
Dimensionless
Decay factor per chunk index of exponential temporal-ensembling weights; its size sets how fast newer chunks enter the blend.


\(\ImitationLearnedPolicy\)
Imitation-Learned Policy
Function
Policy learned from expert demonstrations or expert-labeled states, compared against the expert policy; indexed by aggregation round in DAgger.


\(\LatentKlWeight\)
Latent KL Weight
Dimensionless
Weight on the KL divergence between the latent posterior and prior in a conditional variational autoencoder objective; not the RLHF reference penalty coefficient.


\(\LatentPosteriorDistribution\)
Latent Posterior Distribution
Distribution
Distribution over the latent style variable that a conditional VAE encoder infers from a demonstration chunk and its observation; compared with \(\Glyph{p}\) in the KL term.


\(\MixtureComponentCount\)
Mixture Component Count
Dimensionless
Number of components of a mixture distribution.


\(\MixtureComponentIndex\)
Mixture Component Index
Index
Position of one component of a mixture distribution, from one to the component count \(\MixtureComponentCount\); it indexes the weight, mean, and covariance of a mixture density network.


\(\MixtureComponentMean\)
Mixture Component Mean
Varies
Mean vector of one component of a Gaussian mixture, output by a mixture density network for the given input.


\(\MixtureComponentCovariance\)
Mixture Component Covariance
Varies
Covariance matrix of one component of a Gaussian mixture, output by a mixture density network for the given input.


\(\ObservationEncodingTime\)
Observation Encoding Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time to encode one observation, visual backbone and proprioception, once per policy proposal; the first term of the proposal latency.


\(\ObservationHistoryWindow\)
Observation History Window
Varies
Sliding window of the robot’s most recent onboard observations, from the history length before the current step up to the current step; one row per observation step.


\(\ObservationHistoryLength\)
Observation history length
Steps
Number of past steps the observation history window holds before the current one.


\(\RobotAction\)
Robot Action
Vector
Action vector a learned robot policy emits, written without a step index as the argument of a policy, value function, or action distribution; the same quantity as the cognitive policy action, which carries the step index.


\(\RobotObservation\)
Robot Observation
Vector
Observation vector a robot policy receives from its sensors, written without a step index.


\(\RequestedActionTap\)
Requested Action Tap
Record
First stream of the four-stream action tap, the raw policy or operator request before kinematic mapping.


\(\SuccessorActionVector\)
Successor Action Vector
Vector
Continuous action vector taken in the successor state of a transition, the next action a Bellman backup evaluates.


\(\ReturnStepOffset\)
Return Step Offset
Index
Number of control steps after the current step at which a reward arrives, the summation index of a discounted return.


\(\RolloutHorizon\)
Rollout Horizon
Dimensionless
Number of control steps in one executed rollout, the index of its final state; a step count, not a duration.


\(\RolloutPolicyParameters\)
Rollout Policy Parameters
Vector
Parameters of the policy that collected the current batch of rollouts, frozen while the updated parameters are optimized; the denominator policy of the probability ratio.


\(\PpoClippedSurrogateObjective\)
PPO Clipped Surrogate Objective
Dimensionless
Clipped surrogate objective that proximal policy optimization maximizes, the empirical mean of the smaller of the ratio-weighted advantage and its clipped counterpart; a whole-batch objective, not the per-token term of the language model variant.


\(\PrivilegedSimulatorState\)
Privileged Simulator State
Record
Ground-truth simulator quantities such as friction and contact wrenches that a deployed policy cannot measure; a subset of the physical world state exposed by the simulator.


\(\SimulationParameterVector\)
Simulation Parameter Vector
Varies
Physical parameters that define one simulated environment: link masses, centers of mass, friction, joint damping, transport delays, and sensor noise; sampled in domain randomization, with the nominal point marked by a zero subscript.


\(\ProprioceptiveTokenEmbeddings\)
Proprioceptive Token Embeddings
Vector
Token embeddings of the robot’s joint and force state fed to an embodied transformer; one block of the fused multimodal token stream.


\(\StaticDataDistribution\)
Static Data Distribution
Distribution
Fixed data distribution from which a static benchmark draws its held-out examples.


\(\TextTokenEmbeddings\)
Text Token Embeddings
Vector
Token embeddings of the language instruction fed to an embodied transformer, one block of the fused token stream.


\(\VisionTokenEmbeddings\)
Vision Token Embeddings
Vector
Token embeddings an embodied transformer computes from camera images, one block of the fused token stream.


\(\VitPatchSize\)
Patch Size
Pixels
Side length of one square image patch a vision transformer tokenizes, typically 14 or 16 pixels.


\(\VitPatchTokenEmbedding\)
Patch Token Embedding
Vector
Latent token embedding a vision transformer forms from one image patch.


\(\CriticReturnEstimate\)
Critic Return Estimate
Dimensionless
Remaining-return estimate a learned critic network predicts for an interaction history; the baseline of PPO, which GRPO replaces with the group mean reward.


\(\DecisionProcessState\)
Decision Process State
Record
Complete environment state of a decision process, including interaction history and variables the agent cannot observe. A record, not a number.


\(\DeviationDisadvantage\)
Deviation Disadvantage
Dimensionless
Largest extra expected cost of one deviation from the reference action followed by reference recovery, at any state the learner can reach; an assumption about the task, in normalized cost units.


\(\DiscountFactor\)
Discount Factor
Dimensionless
Factor by which a reward arriving one step later is weighted in the return, between zero and one; one means undiscounted.


\(\EnvironmentTransitionDistribution\)
Environment Transition Distribution
Distribution
Distribution the environment induces over the next state given the current state and the action taken.


\(\EstimatedHistoryAdvantage\)
Estimated History Advantage
Dimensionless
Estimate of how much an action taken after a given interaction history beats the policy value at that history.


\(\ExpectedHistoryActionReturn\)
Expected History-Action Return
Function
Expected remaining return under a policy after taking a given action at a given interaction history and then following the policy.


\(\ExpectedRemainingReturn\)
Expected Remaining Return
Function
Expected remaining return under a policy from a given interaction history at a decision step; written with the policy as a superscript.


\(\ExpectedReturnObjective\)
Expected Return Objective
Function
Expected return of a policy as a function of its parameters, the objective reinforcement learning maximizes. Not the imitation cost sum \(\ExpectedTaskCostSum\).


\(\ExpectedTaskCostSum\)
Expected Task Cost Sum
Function
Expected sum over the horizon of the normalized immediate task costs a policy incurs; the imitation bounds compare it for a learner and the reference. Not monetary.

title: Notation
text:
Response-time analysis keeps the Liu–Layland letters of its literature, but only inside that model and only with a task index \(\Glyph{i}\), \(\Glyph{j}\), or \(\Glyph{k}\). The letters are \(\WorstCaseExecutionTime_i\) (worst-case execution time), \(\TaskBlockingTime_i\) (blocking), \(\TaskInterferenceTime_i\) (interference), \(\Glyph{J}_i\) (release jitter), \(\TaskPeriod_i\) (period), \(\WorstCaseResponseTime_i\) (worst-case response time), and \(\TaskRelativeDeadline_i\) (relative deadline, which is \(\CompletionDeadline\) of task \(\Glyph{i}\) in the series’ terms). They combine as in \(\WorstCaseResponseTime_i = \WorstCaseExecutionTime_i + \TaskBlockingTime_i + \TaskInterferenceTime_i \le \TaskRelativeDeadline_i\). Outside that model these letters keep their table meanings.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\PowerRailInductance, \PowerRailResistance\)
Power Rail Inductance / ESR
\(\MicroUnitPrefix\text{H}, \text{m}\OhmUnit\)
Parasitic inductance and equivalent series resistance of the power harness feeding the inverter; with \(\DcBusBulkCapacitance\) they set the droop \(\Glyph{\Delta V_{\text{droop}}}\) under a current step.


\(\DcBusBulkCapacitance\)
DC Bus Bulk Capacitance
\(\MicroUnitPrefix\text{F}\)
Inverter decoupling capacitor bank buffering transient inductive voltage collapse.


\(\MemoryBusQueueDelay\)
Memory Bus Queue Delay
\(\text{ms}\)
Contention latency \(\sum_{\Glyph{k}} {\DataVolume}_{\Glyph{k}} / \Glyph{\text{BW}_{\text{peak}}} + \Glyph{N_{\text{conflict}}} \BankConflictPenalty\) across shared SoC crossbars.


\(\TelemetryFreshnessBound\)
Telemetry Freshness Bound
\(\text{ms}\)
Maximum allowable age of sensor telemetry before an interlock trips: \(\TelemetryFreshnessBound \le \PositionErrorCeiling / \SpeedBound\).


\(\ClockOffset\)
Clock Offset
\(\MicroUnitPrefix\text{s}\)
Offset of one clock from another, estimated from a timestamp exchange as \(\ClockOffset = [(\TimeInstant_2 - \TimeInstant_1) - (\TimeInstant_4 - \TimeInstant_3)]/2\); its one-way path delay is \(\PtpPropagationDelay\).


\(\TimingJitter\)
Timing Jitter
\(\MicroUnitPrefix\text{s}\)
Standard deviation of a nominally periodic event’s timing about its schedule.


\(\SynchronizationBlackout\)
Synchronization Blackout
\(\text{s}\)
Interval during which a node receives no synchronization message and free-runs on its own clock.


\(\AcquisitionEpoch\)
Acquisition Epoch
\(\text{s}\)
Instant a sensor transduced one observation, such as a camera frame's exposure midpoint or an encoder latch; the evidence epoch of a belief is the latest acquisition epoch among the measurements that constrained it.


\(\ActuatorOffTime\)
Actuator Recovery Time
\(\text{s}\)
Recovery duration between actuator bursts in one duty cycle; the burst itself is \(\ActuatorOnTime\).


\(\ActuatorOnTime\)
Actuator Burst Time
\(\text{s}\)
Duration an actuator runs at burst power in one duty cycle; pairs with the recovery time \(\ActuatorOffTime\).


\(\AisleTravelSpeed\)
Aisle Travel Speed
\(\text{m/s}\)
Speed the mobile base is set to travel in a warehouse aisle, chosen below the derived dry-floor speed ceiling; it is the speed at detection in the aisle stopping budget.


\(\ArrivalTimestamp\)
Arrival Timestamp
\(\text{s}\)
Instant a sensor sample arrives in host memory, when its direct memory access transfer completes; later than the capture timestamp by exposure, readout, transport, and transfer.


\(\AvailableBrakingDistance\)
Available Braking Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Clear distance minus the localization bound and the protective clearance margin; the distance braking and blind travel may use.


\(\AvailableDeceleration\)
Available Deceleration
\(\text{m/s}^2\)
Deceleration a machine actually has, the smaller of its credible braking deceleration and the traction limit, friction coefficient times \(\Gravity\).


\(\BankConflictPenalty\)
Bank Conflict Penalty
\(\text{s}\)
Time one memory bank or row conflict adds to a queued transfer, about a precharge plus an activation.


\(\BlindTravelDistance\)
Blind Travel Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a machine travels during the pre-brake delay, before retarding force begins: speed at detection times that delay.


\(\BrakeChopperResistance\)
Brake Chopper Resistance
\(\OhmUnit\)
Resistance of the absorption resistor a dynamic brake chopper switches across the bus; must dissipate the peak regenerated power at the clamp voltage.


\(\BrakingDistance\)
Braking Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a machine travels from brake onset to rest, speed squared over twice the credible deceleration; excludes travel during the pre-brake delay.


\(\CaptureTimestamp\)
Capture Timestamp
\(\text{s}\)
Midpoint of the sensor’s exposure or firing window, the instant the observation describes; the letter t carrying index zero.


\(\CaseTemperature\)
Case Temperature
\(^\circ\text{C}\)
Temperature of a motor or package case.


\(\CaseThermalTimeConstant\)
Case Thermal Time Constant
\(\text{s}\)
Thermal time constant of the motor case stage of a multi-node motor thermal model.


\(\ChopperClampVoltage\)
Chopper Clamp Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Bus voltage at which a dynamic brake chopper switches its absorption resistor across the bus; above the full-charge voltage and below the converter and switch ratings.


\(\ClockConversionBound\)
Clock Conversion Bound
\(\text{s}\)
Bound on the error of converting a sensor’s capture timestamp to the clock of the safety microcontroller that hosts the permission path; measured from offset tails, path asymmetry, and drift, and added to the observation age at dispatch.


\(\ClockConversionIntercept\)
Clock Conversion Intercept
\(\text{s}\)
Intercept of the affine mapping that converts a capture-clock time to the safety microcontroller’s clock.


\(\ClockConversionSlope\)
Clock Conversion Slope
Dimensionless
Slope of the affine mapping that converts a capture-clock time to the safety microcontroller’s clock; near one, the drift between the clocks.


\(\ConsoleCommunicationTime\)
Console Communication Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time the operator console and link add to a takeover: video transport to the operator plus the returning protocol exchange; shares its glyph with the gradient communication time of training, a different quantity.


\(\ConstantHazardRate\)
Constant Hazard Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Constant rate of hazardous failures per operating hour of a machine, the rate a failure-free test exposure bounds from above; assumes the flat middle of the bathtub curve.


\(\ConverterLockoutVoltage\)
Converter Lockout Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Input voltage at which a DC-DC converter shuts off (undervoltage lockout); bus droop below it resets the computation the converter supplies.


\(\CopperReferenceTemperature\)
Copper Reference Temperature
°C
Temperature at which a winding has its reference resistance, the base of the copper temperature coefficient.


\(\CopperTemperatureCoefficient\)
Copper Temperature Coefficient
\(\text{K}^{-1}\)
Fractional rise in a copper winding’s resistance per kelvin; about 0.00393 per kelvin for annealed copper at 20 °C.


\(\CopperThermalTimeConstant\)
Copper Thermal Time Constant
\(\text{s}\)
Thermal time constant of the winding copper stage in a multi-node motor thermal model.


\(\CoreAmbientThermalResistance\)
Core-to-Ambient Thermal Resistance
\(\text{K/W}\)
Convective thermal resistance from a motor’s stator core to the ambient air; it rises when an enclosure removes airflow.


\(\EquilibriumWindingTemperature\)
Equilibrium Winding Temperature
°C
Temperature a winding approaches asymptotically under a constant loss power: ambient plus loss power times the thermal resistance in the first-order model.


\(\DcBusVoltage\)
DC Bus Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Voltage of the DC bus that feeds a motor inverter.


\(\DcRailVoltage\)
DC Rail Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Voltage of the shared DC power rail that feeds the compute and the motor inverters; the bus of \(\DcBusVoltage\) is the inverter’s side of it.


\(\DroopedSupplyVoltage\)
Drooped Supply Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Supply voltage a core sees at the bottom of a droop event.


\(\FinalBusVoltage\)
Final Bus Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
DC bus voltage at the end of a regenerative stop when the bus capacitance alone absorbs the returned energy; a screening endpoint, since exceeding a component rating means the stop needs another energy path.


\(\GatePropagationDelay\)
Gate Propagation Delay
\(\text{s}\)
Propagation delay of a logic gate as a function of its supply voltage; the alpha-power law makes it grow as the supply approaches the transistor threshold voltage.


\(\HeatDissipationPower\)
Heat Dissipation Power
\(\text{W}\)
Power the hardware at one signal handoff dissipates as heat, the energy-and-heat limit of the handoff matrix; from under a watt on the safety microcontroller to tens of watts on the proposer accelerators.


\(\DeadlineInstant\)
Deadline Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Clock instant by which an observation or action must be complete.


\(\FallbackDeadline\)
Fallback Deadline
\(\text{s}\)
Latest permissible wait after a handover request before the fallback must begin, from the stopping inequality at the current speed and clearance; it clips the handover timeout ceiling \(\HandoverTimeoutCeiling\).


\(\HandoverTimeoutCeiling\)
Handover Timeout Ceiling
\(\text{s}\)
Configured protocol ceiling on the handover timeout, which the clearance-derived \(\FallbackDeadline\) may shorten but never extend.


\(\EnforcedCommandTap\)
Enforced Command Tap
Record
Third stream of the four-stream action tap, the command the permission check admitted.


\(\InitialBusVoltage\)
Initial Bus Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
DC bus voltage at the moment a regenerative deceleration begins; the worst case is a full pack, when the battery refuses charge.


\(\NominalSupplyVoltage\)
Nominal Supply Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Nominal regulated supply voltage of a core rail.


\(\InverterCurrentLimit\)
Inverter Current Limit
\(\text{A}\)
Largest current an inverter bridge lets flow, set to protect its transistors and the stator.


\(\LoadCurrent\)
Load Current
\(\text{A}\)
Current the loads draw from a bus node.


\(\JunctionTemperature\)
Junction Temperature
\(\text{°C}\)
Temperature of a silicon die at its transistor junctions; written as a function of time when it relaxes after a power step. A temperature always carries a subscript, since the bare letter is time.


\(\JunctionCaseThermalResistance\)
Junction-to-Case Thermal Resistance
\(\text{K/W}\)
Thermal resistance from a silicon junction to the case of its package.


\(\JunctionAmbientThermalResistance\)
Junction-to-Ambient Thermal Resistance
\(\text{K/W}\)
Lumped thermal resistance from a silicon junction to the ambient air, the sum of the junction-to-case, interface-material, and chassis paths; not the motor stator-to-ambient path.


\(\OhmUnit\)
Ohm Unit
Unit
SI unit of electrical resistance, written upright after a prefix as in milliohms.


\(\PeriodicTaskCount\)
Periodic Task Count
Dimensionless
Number of periodic tasks in a real-time task set; it sets the Liu and Layland utilization bound, which falls toward the natural logarithm of two as the count grows.


\(\MicrocontrollerClockTime\)
Microcontroller Clock Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time read on the safety microcontroller’s monotonic clock.


\(\MappedCommandTap\)
Mapped Command Tap
Record
Second stream of the four-stream action tap, the kinematically mapped command before it crosses to the safety microcontroller.


\(\MeasuredResponseTap\)
Measured Response Tap
Record
Fourth stream of the four-stream action tap, the plant response measured by joint encoders and current shunts.


\(\LeaseAdmissionInstant\)
Lease Admission Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant at which the permission path admits an intent lease, the start of its validity interval.


\(\NominalPlanExpiry\)
Nominal Plan Expiry
\(\text{s}\)
Instant, on the permission clock, at which the nominal setpoints of an admitted trajectory record end; never executed when the matched stop begins at commitment.


\(\ObservationAgeBudget\)
Observation Age Budget
\(\text{s}\)
Configured upper bound on observation age above which a consumer refuses a state.


\(\MaximumObservationAge\)
Maximum Observation Age
\(\text{s}\)
Largest observation age a consumer tolerates before acting on the observation is no longer safe or stable; the phase-margin ceiling in the control chapters and the freshness threshold in the memory and machine-learning chapters.


\(\MissionDuration\)
Mission Duration
\(\text{s}\)
Duration of one mission of a mobile robot, the unit of operation over which a per-mission failure probability is allocated.


\(\MissionEnergy\)
Mission Energy
\(\text{J}\)
Total energy a machine draws to complete one physical mission; distinct from the machine-learning workload’s total energy.


\(\OperatorSensoryTime\)
Operator Sensory Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time an operator needs to perceive a takeover stimulus, the perceptual stage of a simple reaction (Model Human Processor perceptual cycle).


\(\OperatorCognitiveTime\)
Operator Cognitive Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time an operator needs to decide on a response to a takeover stimulus, the cognitive stage of a simple reaction (Model Human Processor cognitive cycle).


\(\OperatorMotorTime\)
Operator Motor Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time an operator needs to move the controls once a response is chosen, the motor stage of a simple reaction; not the electrical time of a motor.


\(\OperatorStabilizationInstant\)
Operator Stabilization Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Time after a takeover at which the operator’s corrections settle into a steady return toward the nominal corridor.


\(\OrientationTolerance\)
Orientation Tolerance
\(\text{rad}\)
Largest angular orientation error a task accepts.


\(\ObservedCycleCount\)
Observed Cycle Count
Dimensionless
Number of operating cycles, each one observation of the monitored quantity, over which exceedances are counted.


\(\ObservedTrialFailureCount\)
Observed Trial Failure Count
Dimensionless
Number of failures observed among the trials of a test campaign, fixed-sample or sequential.


\(\OperationalTestDistribution\)
Operational Test Distribution
Distribution
Declared joint distribution of trial conditions an evaluation campaign samples, the population its success probability describes; each stratum of a stratified test matrix is its own distribution, and it is not a dataset.


\(\PreTriggerWindowDuration\)
Pre-Trigger Window Duration
\(\text{s}\)
Length of the ring-buffer window before an intervention trigger that the logger freezes and keeps; sized from the out-of-loop takeover latency and rounded up to whole seconds.


\(\PrebrakeDelayCeiling\)
Pre-Brake Delay Ceiling
\(\text{s}\)
Largest pre-brake delay that still lets the machine stop within its clearance: clearance minus margins and braking distance, divided by speed; the ceiling the lease rule subtracts the loop, transport, actuator, and observation times from.


\(\StopDecisionComputeBound\)
Stop Decision Compute Bound
\(\text{s}\)
Bound on the stop-decision computation and any still-required input transfer that a hazard-triggered stop spends inside the pre-brake delay; a budget term, not operations over a sustained rate.


\(\SupervisoryTakeoverLatency\)
Supervisory Takeover Latency
\(\text{s}\)
Total time from a takeover demand to the first checked human command: the human sensory, cognitive, and motor times plus console transport and handshake; the generic form of the in-loop and out-of-loop design values.


\(\RemainingExecutionLease\)
Remaining Execution Lease
\(\text{s}\)
Time left on the active execution lease, the lease length minus the time elapsed since its last accepted renewal; a field of the per-tick evidence tuple.


\(\ReplacementLatency\)
Replacement Latency
\(\text{s}\)
Time from the capture of the observation a candidate trajectory rests on to that candidate’s admission into the execution queue; a latency, not a period, and not the loss that bare \(\Glyph{L}\) names.


\(\SignalHandoff\)
Signal Handoff
Record
One of the five canonical signal handoffs of the machine, from sensing to perception through enforcer to actuator, at which interface limits are budgeted; written with its position.


\(\SynchronizationErrorBound\)
Synchronization Error Bound
\(\text{s}\)
Bound on the error of converting a timestamp from one node’s clock to another’s; the clock-conversion error of the observation contract, not an estimated clock offset.


\(\PtpPropagationDelay\)
PTP Propagation Delay
\(\text{s}\)
One-way network path delay between two clocks, estimated from a symmetric two-way Precision Time Protocol exchange.


\(\RealTimeTaskIndex\)
Real-Time Task Index
Index
Position of one periodic task in a real-time task set, the index of its period, deadline, and execution time; written bare when the text names the task.


\(\TaskBlockingTime\)
Task Blocking Time
\(\text{s}\)
Longest time a real-time task can wait for a lower-priority task to release a shared resource; written with its task index, and under the priority ceiling protocol at most one lower-priority critical section.


\(\ReadStartSequenceCount\)
Read-Start Sequence Count
Dimensionless
Value of a sequence-lock counter that a reader loads before copying the shared slot; the read is valid only if it is even and equals the end count.


\(\ReadEndSequenceCount\)
Read-End Sequence Count
Dimensionless
Value of a sequence-lock counter that a reader loads after copying the shared slot; a change from the start count means a writer preempted the copy and the snapshot is torn.


\(\RowActivationDelay\)
Row Activation Delay
\(\text{s}\)
Minimum time from activating a DRAM row to the first column access to it, the row-to-column delay (JEDEC tRCD).


\(\RowPrechargeTime\)
Row Precharge Time
\(\text{s}\)
Minimum time a DRAM bank needs to close its open row by precharge before another row can be activated (JEDEC tRP); a row conflict costs it plus the row activation delay.


\(\RawHardwareFaultRate\)
Raw Hardware Fault Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Rate of hazardous hardware faults before any diagnostic mitigates them, the sum of the component fault rates; usually quoted in failures in time.


\(\RatedFatigueLife\)
Rated Fatigue Life
Dimensionless
Cumulative load-cycle count at which 10% of a population of identical components is expected to have failed; the subscript ten is part of the symbol.


\(\SourceCurrent\)
Source Current
\(\text{A}\)
Current arriving at a bus node through the source path of battery, harness, and switches; it differs from the load current during a transient, and the bus capacitance supplies the difference.


\(\SourceVoltage\)
Source Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Unloaded voltage of the supply that feeds a bus node through the source path; minus the drop across the rail resistance and inductance it gives the bus voltage.


\(\ReferenceWindingResistance\)
Reference Winding Resistance
\(\Glyph{\Omega}\)
Winding resistance at the reference temperature, the base of copper’s linear resistance law.


\(\StatorCoreTemperature\)
Stator Core Temperature
\(\text{K}\) or \(^\circ\text{C}\)
Temperature of the stator core in a two-node motor thermal model.


\(\ProtectiveSeparationDistance\)
Protective Separation Distance
\(\text{m}\)
Minimum distance a speed-and-separation monitor must keep between a person and a robot; the sum of the human travel, robot reaction travel, robot stopping travel, intrusion, and the two uncertainty terms of ISO/TS 15066.


\(\RobotReactionTravel\)
Robot Reaction Travel
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a robot travels during its reaction time before stopping begins; a term of the protective separation distance.


\(\RobotStoppingTravel\)
Robot Stopping Travel
\(\text{m}\)
Distance a robot travels while stopping; a term of the protective separation distance.


\(\RobotPositionUncertainty\)
Robot Position Uncertainty
\(\text{m}\)
Position uncertainty of the robot; a term of the protective separation distance.


\(\SequentialTrialCount\)
Sequential Trial Count
Dimensionless
Number of trials a sequential test has observed so far, the index of its running log-likelihood ratio.


\(\TailRiskObservation\)
Tail-Risk Observation
Varies
Monitored physical quantity whose rare large values a tail model describes, such as a contact load or a control-loop latency, treated as a random variable; in the unit of the quantity monitored, and indexed for one independent observation.


\(\TailRiskObservationLevel\)
Tail-Risk Observation Level
Varies
Level of the monitored quantity at which its distribution or density is evaluated, or one observed value of it; the lower cutoff of a power-law tail is marked by a zero subscript.


\(\TailShapeParameter\)
Tail Shape Parameter
Dimensionless
Shape parameter of an extreme value tail model, positive for a power-law tail, zero for an exponential tail, and negative for a bounded tail; shared by the generalized extreme value and generalized Pareto models.


\(\TailSupportUpperEndpoint\)
Tail Support Upper Endpoint
Varies
Right endpoint of the support of the monitored quantity’s distribution, possibly infinite; in the unit of the monitored quantity.


\(\TargetExceedanceProbability\)
Target Exceedance Probability
Dimensionless
Per-sample probability of a catastrophic exceedance that a design margin is sized against; a probability per sampled cycle, not a rate per operating hour.


\(\TaskInterferenceTime\)
Task Interference Time
\(\text{s}\)
Processor time that higher-priority tasks and interrupt handlers take from a real-time task within its response window. Written with its task index; it depends on the response time itself, so it is found by a fixed-point recurrence.


\(\TaskPeriod\)
Task Period
\(\text{s}\)
Interval between successive releases of a periodic real-time task, written with its task index.


\(\TaskRelativeDeadline\)
Task Relative Deadline
\(\text{s}\)
Longest time after its release by which a job of a real-time task must complete, written with its task index. The series-wide deadline is \(\CompletionDeadline\).


\(\TaskSetUtilization\)
Task Set Utilization
Dimensionless
Share of processor time a set of periodic real-time tasks demands, the sum over tasks of \(\WorstCaseExecutionTime/\TaskPeriod\).


\(\WorstCaseExecutionTime\)
Worst-Case Execution Time
\(\text{s}\)
Worst-case execution time of one real-time task in response-time analysis; used only inside that analysis and only with a task index.


\(\WorstCaseResponseTime\)
Worst-Case Response Time
\(\text{s}\)
Longest time from a real-time task’s release to its completion; used only with a task index.


\(\TrackingStartInstant\)
Tracking Start Instant
\(\text{s}\)
Instant, on the permission clock, at which nominal tracking of an admitted trajectory record begins; the first of the record’s four deadlines.


\(\TimestampSkew\)
Timestamp Skew
\(\text{s}\)
Skew between the time stamps of two records or clocks. The book writes it with the finite-change prefix, \(\FiniteChange\,\TimestampSkew\).


\(\TrackLastUpdateTime\)
Track Last Update Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time of the most recent observation associated with a track.


\(\CurrentWallClockTime\)
Current Wall-Clock Time
\(\text{s}\)
Wall-clock time at which a monitor evaluates staleness; a point in time, like \(\TimeInstant\), fixed at the moment of the check.


\(\FailureObservationInterval\)
Failure Observation Interval
\(\text{s}\)
Length of the time interval over which failures are counted under the Poisson failure model; a generic window, not the length of one job.


\(\ComponentFailureRate\)
Component Failure Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Rate at which one component fails; the system-wide rate is the component count times this rate under independent, identical components.


\(\UnmitigatedHardwareFaultRate\)
Unmitigated Hardware Fault Rate
\(\text{h}^{-1}\)
Rate of hardware faults whose hazardous effect no diagnostic mitigates, the rate compared with the target hazard rate.


\(\WatchdogEarliestServiceTime\)
Watchdog Earliest Service Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time after the last reload before which a windowed watchdog rejects a service attempt as too early, the lower end of its service window. With \(\WatchdogLatestServiceTime\) it bounds the valid window.


\(\WatchdogLatestServiceTime\)
Watchdog Latest Service Time
\(\text{s}\)
Time after the last reload by which a windowed watchdog must be serviced, past which it trips the safe state.


\(\ThrottleTripTemperature\)
Throttle Trip Temperature
°C
Junction temperature at or above which a hardware thermal governor reduces the processor clock; paired with a lower clear temperature for hysteresis.


\(\TransistorThresholdVoltage\)
Transistor Threshold Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Gate-source voltage at which a transistor begins to conduct. The headroom between supply and threshold sets gate delay in the alpha-power law.


\(\VelocitySaturationExponent\)
Velocity Saturation Exponent
Dimensionless
Technology-dependent exponent of the alpha-power law, by which drain current grows with gate overdrive above threshold; it falls from 2 for a long channel toward 1 as carrier velocity saturates.


\(\WindingCoreThermalResistance\)
Winding-to-Core Thermal Resistance
\(\text{K/W}\)
Conductive thermal resistance from a motor winding to its stator core; in series with the core-to-ambient resistance it makes the total \(\ThermalResistance\).


\(\WindingCurrent\)
Winding Current
\(\text{A}\)
Electric current flowing through a motor winding, which heats it at the rate of current squared times resistance.


\(\ConductorCurrent\)
Conductor Current
\(\text{A}\)
Electrical current flowing through a power-distribution conductor; resistive loss is its square times the conductor resistance.


\(\WindingLossPower\)
Winding Loss Power
\(\text{W}\)
Resistive power dissipated in the motor windings.


\(\WindingTemperatureLimit\)
Winding Temperature Limit
°C
Largest winding temperature the insulation class and derating policy allow.


\(\MicroUnitPrefix\)
Micro Unit Prefix
Prefix
SI prefix for one millionth, written before a unit such as seconds; it only scales the unit after it and is never a quantity, a service rate, or a mean.


\(\SupplyVoltage\)
Supply Voltage
\(\text{V}\)
Voltage that powers a digital circuit and that voltage and frequency scaling lowers; dynamic power scales with \(\SupplyVoltage^2\).


\(\ParasiticLoopInductance\)
Parasitic Loop Inductance
\(\text{H}\)
Unintended inductance of the current loop that feeds an accelerator core rail; it turns current slew into voltage droop.

title: Notation
text:
Embodied robotic platforms increasingly run large multimodal foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) backbones and cross-attention policy decoders, alongside deterministic real-time control stacks. Serving these models on an embedded edge computer requires tracking both the neural architecture dimensions and the memory footprint those dimensions occupy:










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\AttentionHeadDimension\)
Attention Head Dimension
Integer
Per-head hidden dimension in attention layers.


\(\HiddenDimension\)
Hidden Dimension
Integer
Hidden feature (model) width \(\HiddenDimension\) of a transformer layer or representation; the distance to a target, also \(\Glyph{d}\), is \(\TargetTravelDistance\) and appears only in the intent-lease reachability test.


\(\ProbabilityFunction(\cdot)\)
Distribution
Distribution
Probability mass or density \(\ProbabilityFunction(\Glyph{x})\), conditional \(\ProbabilityFunction(\Glyph{y} \mid \Glyph{x})\), or an observation model \(\ProbabilityFunction(\MultimodalObservation \mid \PhysicalWorldState)\); lowercase avoids the collision with \(\Glyph{P}\) (parameter count).


\(\Pr(\Glyph{E})\)
Event Probability
Dimensionless
Probability of an event \(\Glyph{E}\), as in \(\Pr(\text{error by step } \Glyph{t})\); use \(\ProbabilityFunction(\cdot)\) for distributions.


\(\LayerInputWidth, \LayerOutputWidth\)
Layer Input and Output Widths
Integer
Number of input and output features of a dense layer, which holds \(\LayerInputWidth \LayerOutputWidth\) weights.


\(\LearningRate\)
Learning Rate
Scalar
Step size for the optimizer; never bare for hardware efficiency, which is \(\EfficiencyHw\).


\(\LossFunction\)
Loss Function
Scalar
The objective minimized during training; a subscript or superscript names the objective (\(\Glyph{\LossFunction_{\text{MSE}}}\), \(\Glyph{\LossFunction_{\text{chunk}}}\), \(\Glyph{\LossFunction^{\text{CLIP}}}\)).


\(\ModelParameters\)
Model Parameters
Vector
Trainable parameter vector or weights \(\ModelParameters\) of a learned model, such as a policy.


\(\LayerCount\)
Number of Layers
Integer
Total number of layers in a network.


\(\SequenceLength\)
Sequence Length
tokens
Input context or sequence length \(\SequenceLength\) in tokens. The behavioral-cloning horizon \(\BehaviorCloningHorizon\) also renders \(\Glyph{S}\) but counts control steps; the two never share an equation.


\(\WeightMemory\)
Weight Memory
bytes
Memory occupied by model weights (\(\Parameters \times \text{bytes-per-parameter}\)).


\(\ElementStorageSize\)
Element Storage Size
bytes/element
Bytes per stored tensor element at the deployed precision.


\(\ArithmeticIntensity\)
Arithmetic Intensity
FLOP/byte
Operations per byte moved from off-chip memory, \(\Operations/\DataVolume\); it decides whether an evaluation is bound by memory or by compute.


\(\EffectiveSampleSize\)
Effective Sample Size
Dimensionless
Number of independent observations that carry the same information about a mean as a serially correlated stream.


\(\EnvironmentParameters\)
Environment Parameters
Record
External physical variables of one trial or rollout, such as floor friction, illuminance, obstacle geometry, and air temperature; written non-bold, so a record rather than a vector.


\(\EvaluationPredicate\)
Evaluation Predicate
Function
Binary predicate that maps a realized trial trajectory to its task outcome, zero or one.


\(\ExceedanceReturnLevel\)
Exceedance Return Level
Varies
Level of the monitored quantity exceeded with the target probability per sampled cycle; its subscript is that exceedance probability.


\(\ExceedanceThreshold\)
Exceedance Threshold
Varies
High threshold on a performance metric above which peaks-over-threshold modeling fits exceedances; it carries the metric’s units (meters for a distance overshoot).


\(\GeneralizedParetoDistribution\)
Generalized Pareto Distribution
Function
Cumulative distribution function of the excess over a high threshold, parameterized by a scale and a tail shape.


\(\GpdScaleParameter\)
Generalized Pareto Scale
Varies
Scale parameter of the generalized Pareto distribution fitted to exceedances over a threshold.


\(\FailureUpperConfidenceLimit\)
Failure Upper Confidence Limit
Dimensionless
One-sided upper confidence limit on the per-trial failure probability from a finite campaign.


\(\HypothesizedTrialFailureProbability\)
Hypothesized Trial Failure Probability
Dimensionless
Per-trial failure probability a sequential probability ratio test specifies under one of its two hypotheses, indexed 0 for the unacceptable null and 1 for the acceptable alternative.


\(\HazardClassIndex\)
Hazard Class Index
Dimensionless
Index of one defined hazard class.


\(\FleetRobotCount\)
Fleet Robot Count
Dimensionless
Number of robots in a deployed fleet; not the accelerator count of a data center fleet.


\(\GaussianCovarianceMatrix\)
Gaussian Covariance Matrix
Matrix
Covariance matrix of a multivariate Gaussian; entries carry the products of the component units.


\(\GaussianMeanVector\)
Gaussian Mean Vector
Vector
Mean vector of a multivariate Gaussian, paired with \(\GaussianCovarianceMatrix\).


\(\PrefillOperations\)
Prefill Operations
\(\text{FLOP}\)
Arithmetic operations one evaluation’s prefill executes over all of its input tokens; the compute-bound phase of a fresh evaluation, and an instance of the operation count.


\(\ProposerEvaluationRate\)
Proposer Evaluation Rate
\(\text{Hz}\)
Rate of fresh proposer evaluations when every evaluation streams the weights.


\(\SoftmaxFunction\)
Softmax Function
Function
Function that maps a vector of logits to a probability vector that sums to one; normalization by construction, not calibrated confidence, and not the sigmoid.


\(\ModelInput\)
Model Input
Record
Input of one example, the data a model receives to produce a prediction; its label partner is \(\Glyph{\mathbf{y}}\). Not a scalar feature \(\Glyph{x_i}\) of a neuron.


\(\ModelPrediction\)
Model Prediction
Dimensionless
Scalar prediction a model outputs for one example, compared with its label by the loss; the vector of class probabilities is \(\Glyph{\hat{\mathbf{y}}}\).


\(\LogitVector\)
Logit Vector
Vector
Unnormalized score for every class that a classifier outputs before softmax; its entries are \(\OutputLogit\).


\(\OutputLogit\)
Output Logit
Dimensionless
Raw score a model outputs for one class before the softmax, indexed by class as \(\Glyph{z_i}\).


\(\ValidationLoss\)
Validation Loss
Scalar
Loss a trained model incurs on held-out validation data; the outer objective of neural architecture search, never the training loss.


\(\WeightMatrix\)
Weight Matrix
Matrix
Matrix of learned weights one layer multiplies its input by, or the kernel tensor of a convolution layer; a subscript names the layer, as in \(\Glyph{\mathbf{W}_1}\).


\(\FunctionJacobian\)
Function Jacobian
Matrix
Matrix of partial derivatives of a differentiated function’s outputs with respect to its inputs; not the manipulator Jacobian of a robot arm.


\(\ZeroMatrix\)
Zero Matrix or Vector
Matrix
Matrix or vector whose entries are all zero; bold, so it is not the scalar zero.


\(\ImageHeight\)
Image Height
pixels
Number of pixel rows in an image or its segmentation mask; shares its glyph with horizons but counts rows.


\(\ImageWidth\)
Image Width
pixels
Number of pixel columns in an image or its segmentation mask.


\(\IndicatorFunction\)
Indicator Function
Function
Function equal to one when its condition holds and zero otherwise.


\(\KlDivergence\)
KL Divergence
nats or bits
Expected extra code length from encoding one distribution with a code built for another; asymmetric, so \(\Glyph{\KlDivergence(p \lVert q) \ne \KlDivergence(q \lVert p)}\), and distillation uses the teacher-to-student order.


\(\ShannonEntropy\)
Shannon Entropy
bits
Average uncertainty of a probability distribution, the expected negative log probability of its outcomes; the log base sets the unit, base two for bits and natural log for nats.


\(\StatisticalHypothesis\)
Statistical Hypothesis
Record
A hypothesis about a population: \(\Glyph{H_0}\) the null, \(\Glyph{H_1}\) the alternative, and \(\Glyph{H_{(i)}}\) the hypothesis with the \(\Glyph{i}\)-th smallest p-value. A record, not a number.


\(\SignificanceCriticalQuantile\)
Significance Critical Quantile
Dimensionless
Standard-normal quantile at one minus half the significance level, the two-sided critical value of a release test; about 1.96 at a significance level of 0.05.


\(\NextDecisionProcessState\)
Next Decision-Process State
Record
State a decision process moves to after an action is taken in the current state, as in the transition law \(\Glyph{p(s^\prime \mid s, a)}\); the successor of the current state.


\(\PolicyObservedState\)
Policy Observed State
Record
State or observation a policy conditions its choice of action on, the conditioning argument in \(\Glyph{\pi_\theta(a \mid s)}\).


\(\PolicyAction\)
Policy Action
Record
Action a policy chooses given the state it observes, the chosen argument in \(\Glyph{\pi_\theta(a \mid s)}\); agentic rollouts use their own rollout-action symbol.


\(\PolicyProbabilityRatio\)
Policy Probability Ratio
Dimensionless
Ratio of a sampled token’s probability under the current policy to its probability under the behavior policy that generated it; clipped to an interval of half-width \(\RatioClippingWidth\) around one.


\(\RatioClippingWidth\)
Ratio Clipping Width
Dimensionless
Half-width of the interval around one to which the clipped surrogate limits the probability ratio; between zero and one.


\(\PolicyHistoryActionReturn\)
Policy History-Action Return
Dimensionless
Expected remaining return under the current policy after taking a given action at a given interaction history and then following that policy, written \(\Glyph{Q^{\pi}(h_k, a_k)}\).


\(\PolicyRemainingReturn\)
Policy Remaining Return
Dimensionless
Expected remaining return under the current policy from a given interaction history, written \(\Glyph{V^{\pi}(h_k)}\); the baseline the advantage subtracts.


\(\PolicyHistoryAdvantage\)
Policy History Advantage
Dimensionless
Return of a given action at a given interaction history minus the remaining return at that history, \(\Glyph{\PolicyHistoryAdvantage(h_k, a_k) = \PolicyHistoryActionReturn(h_k, a_k) - \PolicyRemainingReturn(h_k)}\).


\(\StateDistribution\)
State Distribution
Distribution
Average distribution of states a policy visits over the horizon; the per-step form carries a superscript, \(\Glyph{d_\pi^t}\).


\(\ReferenceStateDistribution\)
Reference State Distribution
Distribution
Average distribution of states the reference policy visits over the horizon; the reference-policy counterpart of \(\StateDistribution\).


\(\Trajectory\)
Trajectory
Record
Ordered record of the states, actions, and observations of one delegated task, \(\Glyph{\tau = (s_0, a_0, o_1, \dots, s_H)}\); a record, not a number.


\(\ClassCount\)
Class Count
Count
Number of classes a classifier distinguishes, or vocabulary entries it scores; the length of its softmax output.


\(\ExampleLabel\)
Example Label
Record
Label paired with one input, treated as a random variable; a bold form is the label written as a vector.




Latin matrices and vectors are set in bold (\(\Glyph{\mathbf{W}}\), \(\Glyph{\mathbf{x}}\)); scalars, dimensions, indices, and individual matrix entries stay italic (\(\Glyph{N}\), \(\Glyph{d}\), \(\Glyph{i}\), \(\Glyph{W}_{ij}\)). The generic parameter symbol \(\Glyph{\theta}\) is the one conventional exception and stays italic. Local matrix algebra follows the same bold rule: matrix operands are bold (\(\Glyph{\mathbf{A}}\), \(\Glyph{\mathbf{B}}\), \(\Glyph{\mathbf{C}}\)), as in general matrix multiply (GEMM) \(\Glyph{\mathbf{C}}=\Glyph{\alpha} \Glyph{\mathbf{A}}\Glyph{\mathbf{B}}+\Glyph{\beta} \Glyph{\mathbf{C}}\). The bold form marks a matrix operand and is distinct from the italic scalar batch size \(\BatchSize\), which remains batch size in scalar contexts. A GEMM’s scalar dimensions are \(\Glyph{M}\), \(\Glyph{N}\), and \(\Glyph{K}\) (\(\Glyph{\mathbf{A}}\) is \(\Glyph{M} \times \Glyph{K}\), \(\Glyph{\mathbf{B}}\) is \(\Glyph{K} \times \Glyph{N}\)). Asymptotic cost is written \(\mathcal{O}(\cdot)\), which keeps it distinct from the operation count \(\Operations\).

title: Notation
text:
A physical trial is expensive, so the evaluation chapters count carefully. These symbols name the trials themselves, the samples a metric is computed over, and the threshold exceedances that tail estimates are built from.










Symbol
Definition
Unit
Notes




\(\CalibrationExampleCount\)
Calibration Example Count
Count
Number of held-out calibration examples, and so of nonconformity scores, used to set a conformal prediction threshold. Not the quantization calibration set.


\(\EvaluationSampleCount\)
Evaluation Sample Count
Count
Number of examples in the evaluation set over which an accuracy or calibration metric is computed; it sets the sampling error. Not the training set size \(\Glyph{D}\).


\(\DiscreteRandomVariable\)
Discrete Random Variable
Record
Discrete random variable, the uncertain quantity whose outcomes a distribution describes; uppercase for the variable, lowercase for one of its outcomes.


\(\TrialCondition\)
Trial Condition
Record
Condition of one physical trial: initial plant state, environment parameters, plant parameters, computational configuration, and termination protocol; drawn from the operational test distribution.


\(\TrialIndex\)
Trial Index
Index
Position of one physical trial within a learning campaign, counted from one.


\(\TrialSuccessProbability\)
Trial Success Probability
Dimensionless
True probability that one trial succeeds under the declared evaluation protocol and test distribution.


\(\ThresholdExceedanceCount\)
Threshold Exceedance Count
Count
Number of trials whose performance metric exceeds the threshold.


\(\ThresholdExcess\)
Threshold Excess
Varies
Amount by which the monitored quantity exceeds the threshold, one recorded exceedance; it carries the unit of the monitored quantity. Its random-variable form is \(\ThresholdExcessVariable\).


\(\ThresholdExcessVariable\)
Threshold Excess Variable
Varies
Excess of the monitored quantity over the threshold, conditional on exceeding it, treated as a random variable.

title: Notation
text:
Physical units: This book uses SI (metric) units throughout, including meters, kilograms, seconds, watts, and °C, consistent with standard engineering and scientific practice. Where source data was originally reported in imperial units, the book converts to SI and notes the original values parenthetically. A space always separates the number from the unit (for example, 100 ms, 2 TB/s).
Data and memory: This book uses decimal SI prefixes only: KB = \(10^3\) bytes, MB = \(10^6\), GB = \(10^9\), TB = \(10^{12}\). Binary-prefixed units do not appear in prose; model sizes, activation footprints, throughputs, and transfer volumes are reported in decimal units (for example, 2 TB/s, 102 MB). Hardware memory capacities are the one exception: they keep the vendor’s nameplate figure and label. A device modeled here with a binary 80 GB capacity holds \(80 \times 2^{30}\) bytes; usable capacity and allocation headroom remain separate.
Compute: The notation distinguishes operation counts from rates. Total work uses FLOPs (for example, GFLOPs, TFLOPs), while throughput uses FLOP/s with decimal prefixes (for example, GFLOP/s, TFLOP/s).

1 TFLOP = \(10^{12}\) FLOPs
1 TFLOP/s = \(10^{12}\) FLOPs per second
Arithmetic intensity conventionally uses FLOP/byte as a unit ratio (floating-point operations per byte moved). This is a ratio unit, not a total-work symbol or throughput symbol.

Power: Power carries a subscript (\(\Glyph{P_{\text{avg}}}\), \(\Glyph{P_{\text{device}}}\), \(\Glyph{P_{\text{cluster}}}\)); bare \(\Glyph{P}\) remains parameter count.
Latency percentiles: Written p50, p95, and p99 in upright type, inside math as well as in prose.
Currency: Dollar amounts use the dollar sign ($); unless otherwise noted, dollar-denominated costs are U.S. dollars (USD).
Precision:

FP64: Double precision (8 bytes)
FP32: Single precision (4 bytes)
TF32: TensorFloat-32 (19-bit Tensor Core compute mode; inputs and storage remain FP32)
FP16: Half precision (2 bytes, standard range)
BF16: Brain float (2 bytes, wide dynamic range)
FP8: Quarter precision (1 byte, E4M3 or E5M2 format)
FP4: 4-bit floating-point format
INT8: 8-bit integer (1 byte)
INT4: 4-bit integer; lower integer precisions follow the same uppercase INTn pattern (for example, INT3, INT2)

title: Notation
text:
Throughout this book, two single-letter symbols recur in both machine learning equations and hardware performance budgets. The most frequent symbol collisions across the machine learning, control, and embedded systems literatures are resolved as follows:










Symbol
ML Meaning
Systems Meaning
Book Convention




\(\BatchSize\)
Batch Size
Bandwidth
Batch Size. Use \(\Bandwidth\) for bandwidth.


\(\Parameters\)
Parameters
Peak FLOP/s
Parameters. Use \(\PeakRate\) for peak rate.




As a general principle, ML conventions take precedence for single letters, while systems concepts get subscripts or multi-letter symbols. This preserves compatibility with the ML literature while distinguishing the robotics and embedded systems meanings used in this book.
